27040.label: Acts 1:1
27040.text: The first account, O The·ophʹi·lus, I composed about all the things Jesus started both to do and to teach,

27041.label: Acts 1:2
27041.text: until the day that he was taken up, after he had given commandment through holy spirit to the apostles whom he chose.

27042.label: Acts 1:3
27042.text: To these also by many positive proofs he showed himself alive after he had suffered, being seen by them throughout forty days and telling the things about the kingdom of God.

27043.label: Acts 1:4
27043.text: And while he was meeting with them he gave them the orders: “Do not withdraw from Jerusalem, but keep waiting for what the Father has promised, about which YOU heard from me;

27044.label: Acts 1:5
27044.text: because John, indeed, baptized with water, but YOU will be baptized in holy spirit not many days after this.”

27045.label: Acts 1:6
27045.text: When, now, they had assembled, they went asking him: “Lord, are you restoring the kingdom to Israel at this time?”

27046.label: Acts 1:7
27046.text: He said to them: “It does not belong to YOU to get knowledge of the times or seasons which the Father has placed in his own jurisdiction;

27047.label: Acts 1:8
27047.text: but YOU will receive power when the holy spirit arrives upon YOU, and YOU will be witnesses of me both in Jerusalem and in all Ju·deʹa and Sa·marʹi·a and to the most distant part of the earth.”

27048.label: Acts 1:9
27048.text: And after he had said these things, while they were looking on, he was lifted up and a cloud caught him up from their vision.

27049.label: Acts 1:10
27049.text: And as they were gazing into the sky while he was on his way, also, look! two men in white garments stood alongside them,

27050.label: Acts 1:11
27050.text: and they said: “Men of Galʹi·lee, why do YOU stand looking into the sky? This Jesus who was received up from YOU into the sky will come thus in the same manner as YOU have beheld him going into the sky.”

27051.label: Acts 1:12
27051.text: Then they returned to Jerusalem from a mountain called the Mount of Olives, which is near Jerusalem, being a sabbath day’s journey away.

27052.label: Acts 1:13
27052.text: So, when they had entered, they went up into the upper chamber, where they were staying, Peter as well as John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bar·tholʹo·mew and Matthew, James [the son] of Al·phaeʹus and Simon the zealous one, and Judas [the son] of James.

27053.label: Acts 1:14
27053.text: With one accord all these were persisting in prayer, together with some women and Mary the mother of Jesus and with his brothers.

27054.label: Acts 1:15
27054.text: Now during these days Peter rose up in the midst of the brothers and said (the crowd of persons was all together about one hundred and twenty):

27055.label: Acts 1:16
27055.text: “Men, brothers, it was necessary for the scripture to be fulfilled, which the holy spirit spoke beforehand by David’s mouth about Judas, who became a guide to those who arrested Jesus,

27056.label: Acts 1:17
27056.text: because he had been numbered among us and he obtained a share in this ministry.

27057.label: Acts 1:18
27057.text: (This very man, therefore, purchased a field with the wages for unrighteousness, and pitching head foremost he noisily burst in his midst and all his intestines were poured out.

27058.label: Acts 1:19
27058.text: It also became known to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that that field was called in their language A·kelʹda·ma, that is, Field of Blood.)

27059.label: Acts 1:20
27059.text: For it is written in the book of Psalms, ‘Let his lodging place become desolate, and let there be no dweller in it,’ and, ‘His office of oversight let someone else take.’

27060.label: Acts 1:21
27060.text: It is therefore necessary that of the men that assembled with us during all the time in which the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,

27061.label: Acts 1:22
27061.text: starting with his baptism by John and until the day he was received up from us, one of these men should become a witness with us of his resurrection.”

27062.label: Acts 1:23
27062.text: So they put up two, Joseph called Barʹsab·bas, who was surnamed Justus, and Mat·thiʹas.

27063.label: Acts 1:24
27063.text: And they prayed and said: “You, O Jehovah, who know the hearts of all, designate which one of these two men you have chosen,

27064.label: Acts 1:25
27064.text: to take the place of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas deviated to go to his own place.”

27065.label: Acts 1:26
27065.text: So they cast lots over them, and the lot fell upon Mat·thiʹas; and he was reckoned along with the eleven apostles.

27066.label: Acts 2:1
27066.text: Now while the day of the [festival of] Pentecost was in progress they were all together at the same place,

27067.label: Acts 2:2
27067.text: and suddenly there occurred from heaven a noise just like that of a rushing stiff breeze, and it filled the whole house in which they were sitting.

27068.label: Acts 2:3
27068.text: And tongues as if of fire became visible to them and were distributed about, and one sat upon each one of them,

27069.label: Acts 2:4
27069.text: and they all became filled with holy spirit and started to speak with different tongues, just as the spirit was granting them to make utterance.

27070.label: Acts 2:5
27070.text: As it was, there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, reverent men, from every nation of those under heaven.

27071.label: Acts 2:6
27071.text: So, when this sound occurred, the multitude came together and were bewildered, because each one heard them speaking in his own language.

27072.label: Acts 2:7
27072.text: Indeed, they were astonished and began to wonder and say: “See here, all these who are speaking are Gal·i·leʹans, are they not?

27073.label: Acts 2:8
27073.text: And yet how is it we are hearing, each one of us, his own language in which we were born?

27074.label: Acts 2:9
27074.text: Parʹthi·ans and Medes and Eʹlam·ites, and the inhabitants of Mes·o·po·taʹmi·a, and Ju·deʹa and Cap·pa·doʹci·a, Ponʹtus and the [district of] Asia,

27075.label: Acts 2:10
27075.text: and Phrygʹi·a and Pam·phylʹi·a, Egypt and the parts of Libʹy·a, which is toward Cy·reʹne, and sojourners from Rome, both Jews and proselytes,

27076.label: Acts 2:11
27076.text: Creʹtans and Arabians, we hear them speaking in our tongues about the magnificent things of God.”

27077.label: Acts 2:12
27077.text: Yes, they were all astonished and were in perplexity, saying one to another: “What does this thing purport to be?”

27078.label: Acts 2:13
27078.text: However, different ones mocked at them and began to say: “They are full of sweet wine.”

27079.label: Acts 2:14
27079.text: But Peter stood up with the eleven and raised his voice and made this utterance to them: “Men of Ju·deʹa and all YOU inhabitants of Jerusalem, let this be known to YOU and give ear to my sayings.

27080.label: Acts 2:15
27080.text: These [people] are, in fact, not drunk, as YOU suppose, for it is the third hour of the day.

27081.label: Acts 2:16
27081.text: On the contrary, this is what was said through the prophet Joel,

27082.label: Acts 2:17
27082.text: ‘“And in the last days,” God says, “I shall pour out some of my spirit upon every sort of flesh, and YOUR sons and YOUR daughters will prophesy and YOUR young men will see visions and YOUR old men will dream dreams;

27083.label: Acts 2:18
27083.text: and even upon my men slaves and upon my women slaves I will pour out some of my spirit in those days, and they will prophesy.

27084.label: Acts 2:19
27084.text: And I will give portents in heaven above and signs on earth below, blood and fire and smoke mist;

27085.label: Acts 2:20
27085.text: the sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and illustrious day of Jehovah arrives.

27086.label: Acts 2:21
27086.text: And everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved.”’

27087.label: Acts 2:22
27087.text: “Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ, a man publicly shown by God to YOU through powerful works and portents and signs that God did through him in YOUR midst, just as YOU yourselves know,

27088.label: Acts 2:23
27088.text: this [man], as one delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God, YOU fastened to a stake by the hand of lawless men and did away with.

27089.label: Acts 2:24
27089.text: But God resurrected him by loosing the pangs of death, because it was not possible for him to continue to be held fast by it.

27090.label: Acts 2:25
27090.text: For David says respecting him, ‘I had Jehovah constantly before my eyes; because he is at my right hand that I may never be shaken.

27091.label: Acts 2:26
27091.text: On this account my heart became cheerful and my tongue rejoiced greatly. Moreover, even my flesh will reside in hope;

27092.label: Acts 2:27
27092.text: because you will not leave my soul in Haʹdes, neither will you allow your loyal one to see corruption.

27093.label: Acts 2:28
27093.text: You have made life’s ways known to me, you will fill me with good cheer with your face.’

27094.label: Acts 2:29
27094.text: “Men, brothers, it is allowable to speak with freeness of speech to YOU concerning the family head David, that he both deceased and was buried and his tomb is among us to this day.

27095.label: Acts 2:30
27095.text: Therefore, because he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath that he would seat one from the fruitage of his loins upon his throne,

27096.label: Acts 2:31
27096.text: he saw beforehand and spoke concerning the resurrection of the Christ, that neither was he forsaken in Haʹdes nor did his flesh see corruption.

27097.label: Acts 2:32
27097.text: This Jesus God resurrected, of which fact we are all witnesses.

27098.label: Acts 2:33
27098.text: Therefore because he was exalted to the right hand of God and received the promised holy spirit from the Father, he has poured out this which YOU see and hear.

27099.label: Acts 2:34
27099.text: Actually David did not ascend to the heavens, but he himself says, ‘Jehovah said to my Lord: “Sit at my right hand,

27100.label: Acts 2:35
27100.text: until I place your enemies as a stool for your feet.”’

27101.label: Acts 2:36
27101.text: Therefore let all the house of Israel know for a certainty that God made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom YOU impaled.”

27102.label: Acts 2:37
27102.text: Now when they heard this they were stabbed to the heart, and they said to Peter and the rest of the apostles: “Men, brothers, what shall we do?”

27103.label: Acts 2:38
27103.text: Peter [said] to them: “Repent, and let each one of YOU be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for forgiveness of YOUR sins, and YOU will receive the free gift of the holy spirit.

27104.label: Acts 2:39
27104.text: For the promise is to YOU and to YOUR children and to all those afar off, just as many as Jehovah our God may call to him.”

27105.label: Acts 2:40
27105.text: And with many other words he bore thorough witness and kept exhorting them, saying: “Get saved from this crooked generation.”

27106.label: Acts 2:41
27106.text: Therefore those who embraced his word heartily were baptized, and on that day about three thousand souls were added.

27107.label: Acts 2:42
27107.text: And they continued devoting themselves to the teaching of the apostles and to sharing [with one another], to taking of meals and to prayers.

27108.label: Acts 2:43
27108.text: Indeed, fear began to fall upon every soul, and many portents and signs began to occur through the apostles.

27109.label: Acts 2:44
27109.text: All those who became believers were together in having all things in common,

27110.label: Acts 2:45
27110.text: and they went selling their possessions and properties and distributing the [proceeds] to all, just as anyone would have the need.

27111.label: Acts 2:46
27111.text: And day after day they were in constant attendance at the temple with one accord, and they took their meals in private homes and partook of food with great rejoicing and sincerity of heart,

27112.label: Acts 2:47
27112.text: praising God and finding favor with all the people. At the same time Jehovah continued to join to them daily those being saved.

27113.label: Acts 3:1
27113.text: Now Peter and John were going up into the temple for the hour of prayer, the ninth hour,

27114.label: Acts 3:2
27114.text: and a certain man that was lame from his mother’s womb was being carried, and they would daily put him near the temple door that was called Beautiful, in order to ask gifts of mercy from those entering into the temple.

27115.label: Acts 3:3
27115.text: When he caught sight of Peter and John about to go into the temple he began requesting to get gifts of mercy.

27116.label: Acts 3:4
27116.text: But Peter, together with John, gazed at him and said: “Take a look at us.”

27117.label: Acts 3:5
27117.text: So he fixed his attention upon them, expecting to get something from them.

27118.label: Acts 3:6
27118.text: However, Peter said: “Silver and gold I do not possess, but what I do have is what I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ the Naz·a·reneʹ, walk!”

27119.label: Acts 3:7
27119.text: With that he took hold of him by the right hand and raised him up. Instantly the soles of his feet and his anklebones were made firm;

27120.label: Acts 3:8
27120.text: and, leaping up, he stood up and began walking, and he entered with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.

27121.label: Acts 3:9
27121.text: And all the people got sight of him walking and praising God.

27122.label: Acts 3:10
27122.text: Moreover, they began to recognize him, that this was the man that used to sit for gifts of mercy at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they became filled with astonishment and ecstasy at what had happened to him.

27123.label: Acts 3:11
27123.text: Well, as the man was holding onto Peter and John, all the people ran together to them at what was called Solʹo·mon’s colonnade, surprised out of their wits.

27124.label: Acts 3:12
27124.text: When Peter saw this, he said to the people: “Men of Israel, why are YOU wondering over this, or why are YOU gazing at us as though by personal power or godly devotion we have made him walk?

27125.label: Acts 3:13
27125.text: The God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob, the God of our forefathers, has glorified his Servant, Jesus, whom YOU, for YOUR part, delivered up and disowned before Pilate’s face, when he had decided to release him.

27126.label: Acts 3:14
27126.text: Yes, YOU disowned that holy and righteous one, and YOU asked for a man, a murderer, to be freely granted to YOU,

27127.label: Acts 3:15
27127.text: whereas YOU killed the Chief Agent of life. But God raised him up from the dead, of which fact we are witnesses.

27128.label: Acts 3:16
27128.text: Consequently his name, by [our] faith in his name, has made this man strong whom YOU behold and know, and the faith that is through him has given the man this complete soundness in the sight of all of YOU.

27129.label: Acts 3:17
27129.text: And now, brothers, I know that YOU acted in ignorance, just as YOUR rulers also did.

27130.label: Acts 3:18
27130.text: But in this way God has fulfilled the things he announced beforehand through the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ would suffer.

27131.label: Acts 3:19
27131.text: “Repent, therefore, and turn around so as to get YOUR sins blotted out, that seasons of refreshing may come from the person of Jehovah

27132.label: Acts 3:20
27132.text: and that he may send forth the Christ appointed for YOU, Jesus,

27133.label: Acts 3:21
27133.text: whom heaven, indeed, must hold within itself until the times of restoration of all things of which God spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets of old time.

27134.label: Acts 3:22
27134.text: In fact, Moses said, ‘Jehovah God will raise up for YOU from among YOUR brothers a prophet like me. YOU must listen to him according to all the things he speaks to YOU.

27135.label: Acts 3:23
27135.text: Indeed, any soul that does not listen to that Prophet will be completely destroyed from among the people.’

27136.label: Acts 3:24
27136.text: And all the prophets, in fact, from Samuel on and those in succession, just as many as have spoken, have also plainly declared these days.

27137.label: Acts 3:25
27137.text: YOU are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant which God covenanted with YOUR forefathers, saying to Abraham, ‘And in your seed all the families of the earth will be blessed.’

27138.label: Acts 3:26
27138.text: To YOU first God, after raising up his Servant, sent him forth to bless YOU by turning each one away from YOUR wicked deeds.”

27139.label: Acts 4:1
27139.text: Now while the [two] were speaking to the people, the chief priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,

27140.label: Acts 4:2
27140.text: being annoyed because they were teaching the people and were plainly declaring the resurrection from the dead in the case of Jesus;

27141.label: Acts 4:3
27141.text: and they laid their hands upon them and put them in custody till the next day, for it was already evening.

27142.label: Acts 4:4
27142.text: However, many of those who had listened to the speech believed, and the number of the men became about five thousand.

27143.label: Acts 4:5
27143.text: The next day there took place in Jerusalem the gathering together of their rulers and older men and scribes

27144.label: Acts 4:6
27144.text: (also Anʹnas the chief priest and Caʹia·phas and John and Alexander and as many as were of the chief priest’s kinsfolk),

27145.label: Acts 4:7
27145.text: and they stood them in their midst and began to inquire: “By what power or in whose name did YOU do this?”

27146.label: Acts 4:8
27146.text: Then Peter, filled with holy spirit, said to them: “Rulers of the people and older men,

27147.label: Acts 4:9
27147.text: if we are this day being examined, on the basis of a good deed to an ailing man, as to by whom this man has been made well,

27148.label: Acts 4:10
27148.text: let it be known to all of YOU and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ the Naz·a·reneʹ, whom YOU impaled but whom God raised up from the dead, by this one does this man stand here sound in front of YOU.

27149.label: Acts 4:11
27149.text: This is ‘the stone that was treated by YOU builders as of no account that has become the head of the corner.’

27150.label: Acts 4:12
27150.text: Furthermore, there is no salvation in anyone else, for there is not another name under heaven that has been given among men by which we must get saved.”

27151.label: Acts 4:13
27151.text: Now when they beheld the outspokenness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were men unlettered and ordinary, they got to wondering. And they began to recognize about them that they used to be with Jesus;

27152.label: Acts 4:14
27152.text: and as they were looking at the man that had been cured standing with them, they had nothing to say in rebuttal.

27153.label: Acts 4:15
27153.text: So they commanded them to go outside the Sanʹhe·drin hall, and they began consulting with one another,

27154.label: Acts 4:16
27154.text: saying: “What shall we do with these men? Because, for a fact, a noteworthy sign has occurred through them, one manifest to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and we cannot deny it.

27155.label: Acts 4:17
27155.text: Nevertheless, in order that it may not be spread abroad further among the people, let us tell them with threats not to speak anymore upon the basis of this name to any man at all.”

27156.label: Acts 4:18
27156.text: With that they called them and charged them, nowhere to make any utterance or to teach upon the basis of the name of Jesus.

27157.label: Acts 4:19
27157.text: But in reply Peter and John said to them: “Whether it is righteous in the sight of God to listen to YOU rather than to God, judge for yourselves.

27158.label: Acts 4:20
27158.text: But as for us, we cannot stop speaking about the things we have seen and heard.”

27159.label: Acts 4:21
27159.text: So, when they had further threatened them, they released them, since they did not find any ground on which to punish them and on account of the people, because they were all glorifying God over what had occurred;

27160.label: Acts 4:22
27160.text: for the man upon whom this sign of healing had occurred was more than forty years old.

27161.label: Acts 4:23
27161.text: After being released they went to their own people and reported what things the chief priests and the older men had said to them.

27162.label: Acts 4:24
27162.text: Upon hearing this they with one accord raised their voices to God and said: “Sovereign Lord, you are the One who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things in them,

27163.label: Acts 4:25
27163.text: and who through holy spirit said by the mouth of our forefather David, your servant, ‘Why did nations become tumultuous and peoples meditate upon empty things?

27164.label: Acts 4:26
27164.text: The kings of the earth took their stand and the rulers massed together as one against Jehovah and against his anointed one.’

27165.label: Acts 4:27
27165.text: Even so, both Herod and Pontius Pilate with [men of] nations and with peoples of Israel were in actuality gathered together in this city against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed,

27166.label: Acts 4:28
27166.text: in order to do what things your hand and counsel had foreordained to occur.

27167.label: Acts 4:29
27167.text: And now, Jehovah, give attention to their threats, and grant your slaves to keep speaking your word with all boldness,

27168.label: Acts 4:30
27168.text: while you stretch out your hand for healing and while signs and portents occur through the name of your holy servant Jesus.”

27169.label: Acts 4:31
27169.text: And when they had made supplication, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken; and they were one and all filled with the holy spirit and were speaking the word of God with boldness.

27170.label: Acts 4:32
27170.text: Moreover, the multitude of those who had believed had one heart and soul, and not even one would say that any of the things he possessed was his own; but they had all things in common.

27171.label: Acts 4:33
27171.text: Also, with great power the apostles continued giving forth the witness concerning the resurrection of the Lord Jesus; and undeserved kindness in large measure was upon them all.

27172.label: Acts 4:34
27172.text: In fact, there was not one in need among them; for all those who were possessors of fields or houses would sell them and bring the values of the things sold

27173.label: Acts 4:35
27173.text: and they would deposit them at the feet of the apostles. In turn distribution would be made to each one, just as he would have the need.

27174.label: Acts 4:36
27174.text: So Joseph, who was surnamed Barʹna·bas by the apostles, which means, when translated, Son of Comfort, a Levite, a native of Cyʹprus,

27175.label: Acts 4:37
27175.text: possessing a piece of land, sold it and brought the money and deposited it at the feet of the apostles.

27176.label: Acts 5:1
27176.text: However, a certain man, An·a·niʹas by name, together with Sap·phiʹra his wife, sold a possession

27177.label: Acts 5:2
27177.text: and secretly held back some of the price, his wife also knowing about it, and he brought just a part and deposited it at the feet of the apostles.

27178.label: Acts 5:3
27178.text: But Peter said: “An·a·niʹas, why has Satan emboldened you to play false to the holy spirit and to hold back secretly some of the price of the field?

27179.label: Acts 5:4
27179.text: As long as it remained with you did it not remain yours, and after it was sold did it not continue in your control? Why was it that you purposed such a deed as this in your heart? You have played false, not to men, but to God.”

27180.label: Acts 5:5
27180.text: On hearing these words An·a·niʹas fell down and expired. And great fear came over all those hearing of it.

27181.label: Acts 5:6
27181.text: But the younger men rose, wrapped him in cloths, and carried him out and buried him.

27182.label: Acts 5:7
27182.text: Now after an interval of about three hours his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.

27183.label: Acts 5:8
27183.text: Peter said to her: “Tell me, did YOU [two] sell the field for so much?” She said: “Yes, for so much.”

27184.label: Acts 5:9
27184.text: So Peter said to her: “Why was it agreed upon between YOU [two] to make a test of the spirit of Jehovah? Look! The feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”

27185.label: Acts 5:10
27185.text: Instantly she fell down at his feet and expired. When the young men came in they found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her alongside her husband.

27186.label: Acts 5:11
27186.text: Consequently great fear came over the whole congregation and over all those hearing about these things.

27187.label: Acts 5:12
27187.text: Moreover, through the hands of the apostles many signs and portents continued to occur among the people; and they were all with one accord in Solʹo·mon’s colonnade.

27188.label: Acts 5:13
27188.text: True, not a one of the others had the courage to join himself to them; nevertheless, the people were extolling them.

27189.label: Acts 5:14
27189.text: More than that, believers in the Lord kept on being added, multitudes both of men and of women;

27190.label: Acts 5:15
27190.text: so that they brought the sick out even into the broad ways and laid them there upon little beds and cots, in order that, as Peter would go by, at least his shadow might fall upon some one of them.

27191.label: Acts 5:16
27191.text: Also, the multitude from the cities around Jerusalem kept coming together, bearing sick people and those troubled with unclean spirits, and they would one and all be cured.

27192.label: Acts 5:17
27192.text: But the high priest and all those with him, the then existing sect of the Sadducees, rose and became filled with jealousy,

27193.label: Acts 5:18
27193.text: and they laid hands upon the apostles and put them in the public place of custody.

27194.label: Acts 5:19
27194.text: But during the night Jehovah’s angel opened the doors of the prison, brought them out and said:

27195.label: Acts 5:20
27195.text: “Be on YOUR way, and, having taken a stand in the temple, keep on speaking to the people all the sayings about this life.”

27196.label: Acts 5:21
27196.text: After hearing this, they entered into the temple at daybreak and began to teach. Now when the high priest and those with him arrived, they called together the Sanʹhe·drin and all the assembly of older men of the sons of Israel, and they sent out to the jail to have them brought.

27197.label: Acts 5:22
27197.text: But when the officers got there they did not find them in the prison. So they returned and made report,

27198.label: Acts 5:23
27198.text: saying: “The jail we found locked with all security and the guards standing at the doors, but on opening up we found no one inside.”

27199.label: Acts 5:24
27199.text: Well, when both the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they fell into a quandary over these matters as to what this would come to.

27200.label: Acts 5:25
27200.text: But a certain man arrived and reported to them: “Look! The men YOU put in the prison are in the temple, standing and teaching the people.”

27201.label: Acts 5:26
27201.text: Then the captain went off with his officers and proceeded to bring them, but without violence, as they were afraid of being stoned by the people.

27202.label: Acts 5:27
27202.text: So they brought them and stood them in the Sanʹhe·drin hall. And the high priest questioned them

27203.label: Acts 5:28
27203.text: and said: “We positively ordered YOU not to keep teaching upon the basis of this name, and yet, look! YOU have filled Jerusalem with YOUR teaching, and YOU are determined to bring the blood of this man upon us.”

27204.label: Acts 5:29
27204.text: In answer Peter and the [other] apostles said: “We must obey God as ruler rather than men.

27205.label: Acts 5:30
27205.text: The God of our forefathers raised up Jesus, whom YOU slew, hanging him upon a stake.

27206.label: Acts 5:31
27206.text: God exalted this one as Chief Agent and Savior to his right hand, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.

27207.label: Acts 5:32
27207.text: And we are witnesses of these matters, and so is the holy spirit, which God has given to those obeying him as ruler.”

27208.label: Acts 5:33
27208.text: When they heard this, they felt deeply cut and were wanting to do away with them.

27209.label: Acts 5:34
27209.text: But a certain man rose in the Sanʹhe·drin, a Pharisee named Ga·maʹli·el, a Law teacher esteemed by all the people, and gave the command to put the men outside for a little while.

27210.label: Acts 5:35
27210.text: And he said to them: “Men of Israel, pay attention to yourselves as to what YOU intend to do respecting these men.

27211.label: Acts 5:36
27211.text: For instance, before these days Theuʹdas rose, saying he himself was somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined his party. But he was done away with, and all those who were obeying him were dispersed and came to nothing.

27212.label: Acts 5:37
27212.text: After him Judas the Gal·i·leʹan rose in the days of the registration, and he drew off people after him. And yet that man perished, and all those who were obeying him were scattered abroad.

27213.label: Acts 5:38
27213.text: And so, under the present circumstances, I say to YOU, Do not meddle with these men, but let them alone; (because, if this scheme or this work is from men, it will be overthrown;

27214.label: Acts 5:39
27214.text: but if it is from God, YOU will not be able to overthrow them;) otherwise, YOU may perhaps be found fighters actually against God.”

27215.label: Acts 5:40
27215.text: At this they gave heed to him, and they summoned the apostles, flogged them, and ordered them to stop speaking upon the basis of Jesus’ name, and let them go.

27216.label: Acts 5:41
27216.text: These, therefore, went their way from before the Sanʹhe·drin, rejoicing because they had been counted worthy to be dishonored in behalf of his name.

27217.label: Acts 5:42
27217.text: And every day in the temple and from house to house they continued without letup teaching and declaring the good news about the Christ, Jesus.

27218.label: Acts 6:1
27218.text: Now in these days, when the disciples were increasing, a murmuring arose on the part of the Greek-speaking Jews against the Hebrew-speaking Jews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.

27219.label: Acts 6:2
27219.text: So the twelve called the multitude of the disciples to them and said: “It is not pleasing for us to leave the word of God to distribute [food] to tables.

27220.label: Acts 6:3
27220.text: So, brothers, search out for yourselves seven certified men from among YOU, full of spirit and wisdom, that we may appoint them over this necessary business;

27221.label: Acts 6:4
27221.text: but we shall devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”

27222.label: Acts 6:5
27222.text: And the thing spoken was pleasing to the whole multitude, and they selected Stephen, a man full of faith and holy spirit, and Philip and Prochʹo·rus and Ni·caʹnor and Tiʹmon and Parʹme·nas and Nic·o·laʹus, a proselyte of Antioch;

27223.label: Acts 6:6
27223.text: and they placed them before the apostles, and, after having prayed, these laid their hands upon them.

27224.label: Acts 6:7
27224.text: Consequently the word of God went on growing, and the number of the disciples kept multiplying in Jerusalem very much; and a great crowd of priests began to be obedient to the faith.

27225.label: Acts 6:8
27225.text: Now Stephen, full of graciousness and power, was performing great portents and signs among the people.

27226.label: Acts 6:9
27226.text: But certain men rose up of those from the so-called Synagogue of the Freedmen, and of the Cy·reʹni·ans and Alexandrians and of those from Ci·liʹcia and Asia, to dispute with Stephen;

27227.label: Acts 6:10
27227.text: and yet they could not hold their own against the wisdom and the spirit with which he was speaking.

27228.label: Acts 6:11
27228.text: Then they secretly induced men to say: “We have heard him speaking blasphemous sayings against Moses and God.”

27229.label: Acts 6:12
27229.text: And they stirred up the people and the older men and the scribes, and, coming upon him suddenly, they took him by force and led him to the Sanʹhe·drin.

27230.label: Acts 6:13
27230.text: And they brought forward false witnesses, who said: “This man does not stop speaking things against this holy place and against the Law.

27231.label: Acts 6:14
27231.text: For instance, we have heard him say that this Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ will throw down this place and change the customs that Moses handed down to us.”

27232.label: Acts 6:15
27232.text: And as all those sitting in the Sanʹhe·drin gazed at him, they saw that his face was as an angel’s face.

27233.label: Acts 7:1
27233.text: But the high priest said: “Are these things so?”

27234.label: Acts 7:2
27234.text: He said: “Men, brothers and fathers, hear. The God of glory appeared to our forefather Abraham while he was in Mes·o·po·taʹmi·a, before he took up residence in Haʹran,

27235.label: Acts 7:3
27235.text: and he said to him, ‘Go out from your land and from your relatives and come on into the land I shall show you.’

27236.label: Acts 7:4
27236.text: Then he went out from the land of the Chal·deʹans and took up residence in Haʹran. And from there, after his father died, [God] caused him to change his residence to this land in which YOU now dwell.

27237.label: Acts 7:5
27237.text: And yet he did not give him any inheritable possession in it, no, not a footbreadth; but he promised to give it to him as a possession, and after him to his seed, while as yet he had no child.

27238.label: Acts 7:6
27238.text: Moreover, God spoke to this effect, that his seed would be alien residents in a foreign land and [the people] would enslave them and afflict [them] for four hundred years.

27239.label: Acts 7:7
27239.text: ‘And that nation for which they will slave I shall judge,’ God said, ‘and after these things they will come out and will render sacred service to me in this place.’

27240.label: Acts 7:8
27240.text: “He also gave him a covenant of circumcision; and thus he became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve family heads.

27241.label: Acts 7:9
27241.text: And the family heads became jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt. But God was with him,

27242.label: Acts 7:10
27242.text: and he delivered him out of all his tribulations and gave him graciousness and wisdom in the sight of Pharʹaoh king of Egypt. And he appointed him to govern Egypt and his whole house.

27243.label: Acts 7:11
27243.text: But a famine came upon the whole of Egypt and Caʹnaan, even a great tribulation; and our forefathers were not finding any provisions.

27244.label: Acts 7:12
27244.text: But Jacob heard there were foodstuffs in Egypt and he sent our forefathers out the first time.

27245.label: Acts 7:13
27245.text: And during the second time Joseph was made known to his brothers; and the family stock of Joseph became manifest to Pharʹaoh.

27246.label: Acts 7:14
27246.text: So Joseph sent out and called Jacob his father and all his relatives from that place, to the number of seventy-five souls.

27247.label: Acts 7:15
27247.text: Jacob went down into Egypt. And he deceased; and so did our forefathers,

27248.label: Acts 7:16
27248.text: and they were transferred to Sheʹchem and were laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a price with silver money from the sons of Haʹmor in Sheʹchem.

27249.label: Acts 7:17
27249.text: “Just as the time was approaching for [fulfillment of] the promise that God had openly declared to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,

27250.label: Acts 7:18
27250.text: until there rose a different king over Egypt, who did not know of Joseph.

27251.label: Acts 7:19
27251.text: This one used statecraft against our race and wrongfully forced the fathers to expose their infants, that they might not be preserved alive.

27252.label: Acts 7:20
27252.text: In that particular time Moses was born, and he was divinely beautiful. And he was nursed three months in [his] father’s home.

27253.label: Acts 7:21
27253.text: But when he was exposed, the daughter of Pharʹaoh picked him up and brought him up as her own son.

27254.label: Acts 7:22
27254.text: Consequently Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians. In fact, he was powerful in his words and deeds.

27255.label: Acts 7:23
27255.text: “Now when the time of his fortieth year was being fulfilled, it came into his heart to make an inspection of his brothers, the sons of Israel.

27256.label: Acts 7:24
27256.text: And when he caught sight of a certain one being unjustly treated, he defended him and executed vengeance for the one being abused by striking the Egyptian down.

27257.label: Acts 7:25
27257.text: He was supposing his brothers would grasp that God was giving them salvation by his hand, but they did not grasp [it].

27258.label: Acts 7:26
27258.text: And the next day he appeared to them as they were fighting, and he tried to bring them together again in peace, saying, ‘Men, YOU are brothers. Why do YOU treat each other unjustly?’

27259.label: Acts 7:27
27259.text: But the one that was treating his neighbor unjustly thrust him away, saying, ‘Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?

27260.label: Acts 7:28
27260.text: You do not want to do away with me in the same manner that you did away with the Egyptian yesterday, do you?’

27261.label: Acts 7:29
27261.text: At this speech Moses took to flight and became an alien resident in the land of Midʹi·an, where he became the father of two sons.

27262.label: Acts 7:30
27262.text: “And when forty years were fulfilled, there appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Siʹnai an angel in the fiery flame of a thornbush.

27263.label: Acts 7:31
27263.text: Now when Moses saw it he marveled at the sight. But as he was approaching to investigate, Jehovah’s voice came,

27264.label: Acts 7:32
27264.text: ‘I am the God of your forefathers, the God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob.’ Seized with trembling, Moses did not dare to investigate further.

27265.label: Acts 7:33
27265.text: Jehovah said to him, ‘Take the sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.

27266.label: Acts 7:34
27266.text: I have certainly seen the wrongful treatment of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning and I have come down to deliver them. And now come, I will send you off to Egypt.’

27267.label: Acts 7:35
27267.text: This Moses, whom they disowned, saying, ‘Who appointed you ruler and judge?’ this man God sent off as both ruler and deliverer by the hand of the angel that appeared to him in the thornbush.

27268.label: Acts 7:36
27268.text: This man led them out after doing portents and signs in Egypt and in the Red Sea and in the wilderness for forty years.

27269.label: Acts 7:37
27269.text: “This is the Moses that said to the sons of Israel, ‘God will raise up for YOU from among YOUR brothers a prophet like me.’

27270.label: Acts 7:38
27270.text: This is he that came to be among the congregation in the wilderness with the angel that spoke to him on Mount Siʹnai and with our forefathers, and he received living sacred pronouncements to give YOU.

27271.label: Acts 7:39
27271.text: To him our forefathers refused to become obedient, but they thrust him aside and in their hearts they turned back to Egypt,

27272.label: Acts 7:40
27272.text: saying to Aaron, ‘Make gods for us to go ahead of us. For this Moses, who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’

27273.label: Acts 7:41
27273.text: So they made a calf in those days and brought up a sacrifice to the idol and began to enjoy themselves in the works of their hands.

27274.label: Acts 7:42
27274.text: So God turned and handed them over to render sacred service to the army of heaven, just as it is written in the book of the prophets, ‘It was not to me that YOU offered victims and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, was it, O house of Israel?

27275.label: Acts 7:43
27275.text: But it was the tent of Moʹloch and the star of the god Reʹphan that YOU took up, the figures which YOU made to worship them. Consequently I will deport YOU beyond Babylon.’

27276.label: Acts 7:44
27276.text: “Our forefathers had the tent of the witness in the wilderness, just as he gave orders when speaking to Moses to make it according to the pattern he had seen.

27277.label: Acts 7:45
27277.text: And our forefathers who succeeded to it also brought it in with Joshua into the land possessed by the nations, whom God thrust out from before our forefathers. Here it remained until the days of David.

27278.label: Acts 7:46
27278.text: He found favor in the sight of God and asked for [the privilege of] providing a habitation for the God of Jacob.

27279.label: Acts 7:47
27279.text: However, Solʹo·mon built a house for him.

27280.label: Acts 7:48
27280.text: Nevertheless, the Most High does not dwell in houses made with hands; just as the prophet says,

27281.label: Acts 7:49
27281.text: ‘The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What sort of house will YOU build for me? Jehovah says. Or what is the place for my resting?

27282.label: Acts 7:50
27282.text: My hand made all these things, did it not?’

27283.label: Acts 7:51
27283.text: “Obstinate men and uncircumcised in hearts and ears, YOU are always resisting the holy spirit; as YOUR forefathers did, so YOU do.

27284.label: Acts 7:52
27284.text: Which one of the prophets did YOUR forefathers not persecute? Yes, they killed those who made announcement in advance concerning the coming of the righteous One, whose betrayers and murderers YOU have now become,

27285.label: Acts 7:53
27285.text: YOU who received the Law as transmitted by angels but have not kept it.”

27286.label: Acts 7:54
27286.text: Well, at hearing these things they felt cut to their hearts and began to gnash their teeth at him.

27287.label: Acts 7:55
27287.text: But he, being full of holy spirit, gazed into heaven and caught sight of God’s glory and of Jesus standing at God’s right hand,

27288.label: Acts 7:56
27288.text: and he said: “Look! I behold the heavens opened up and the Son of man standing at God’s right hand.”

27289.label: Acts 7:57
27289.text: At this they cried out at the top of the voice and put their hands over their ears and rushed upon him with one accord.

27290.label: Acts 7:58
27290.text: And after throwing him outside the city, they began casting stones at him. And the witnesses laid down their outer garments at the feet of a young man called Saul.

27291.label: Acts 7:59
27291.text: And they went on casting stones at Stephen as he made appeal and said: “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”

27292.label: Acts 7:60
27292.text: Then, bending his knees, he cried out with a strong voice: “Jehovah, do not charge this sin against them.” And after saying this he fell asleep [in death].

27293.label: Acts 8:1
27293.text: Saul, for his part, was approving of the murder of him. On that day great persecution arose against the congregation that was in Jerusalem; all except the apostles were scattered throughout the regions of Ju·deʹa and Sa·marʹi·a.

27294.label: Acts 8:2
27294.text: But reverent men carried Stephen to the burial, and they made a great lamentation over him.

27295.label: Acts 8:3
27295.text: Saul, though, began to deal outrageously with the congregation. Invading one house after another and, dragging out both men and women, he would turn them over to prison.

27296.label: Acts 8:4
27296.text: However, those who had been scattered went through the land declaring the good news of the word.

27297.label: Acts 8:5
27297.text: Philip, for one, went down to the city of Sa·marʹi·a and began to preach the Christ to them.

27298.label: Acts 8:6
27298.text: With one accord the crowds were paying attention to the things said by Philip while they listened and looked at the signs he was performing.

27299.label: Acts 8:7
27299.text: For there were many that had unclean spirits, and these would cry out with a loud voice and come out. Moreover, many that were paralyzed and lame were cured.

27300.label: Acts 8:8
27300.text: So there came to be a great deal of joy in that city.

27301.label: Acts 8:9
27301.text: Now in the city there was a certain man named Simon, who, prior to this, had been practicing magical arts and amazing the nation of Sa·marʹi·a, saying he himself was somebody great.

27302.label: Acts 8:10
27302.text: And all of them, from the least to the greatest, would pay attention to him and say: “This man is the Power of God, which can be called Great.”

27303.label: Acts 8:11
27303.text: So they would pay attention to him because of his having amazed them for quite a while by his magical arts.

27304.label: Acts 8:12
27304.text: But when they believed Philip, who was declaring the good news of the kingdom of God and of the name of Jesus Christ, they proceeded to be baptized, both men and women.

27305.label: Acts 8:13
27305.text: Simon himself also became a believer, and, after being baptized, he was in constant attendance upon Philip; and he was amazed at beholding signs and great powerful works taking place.

27306.label: Acts 8:14
27306.text: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Sa·marʹi·a had accepted the word of God, they dispatched Peter and John to them;

27307.label: Acts 8:15
27307.text: and these went down and prayed for them to get holy spirit.

27308.label: Acts 8:16
27308.text: For it had not yet fallen upon any one of them, but they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

27309.label: Acts 8:17
27309.text: Then they went laying their hands upon them, and they began to receive holy spirit.

27310.label: Acts 8:18
27310.text: Now when Simon saw that through the laying on of the hands of the apostles the spirit was given, he offered them money,

27311.label: Acts 8:19
27311.text: saying: “Give me also this authority, that anyone upon whom I lay my hands may receive holy spirit.”

27312.label: Acts 8:20
27312.text: But Peter said to him: “May your silver perish with you, because you thought through money to get possession of the free gift of God.

27313.label: Acts 8:21
27313.text: You have neither part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not straight in the sight of God.

27314.label: Acts 8:22
27314.text: Repent, therefore, of this badness of yours, and supplicate Jehovah that, if possible, the device of your heart may be forgiven you;

27315.label: Acts 8:23
27315.text: for I see you are a poisonous gall and a bond of unrighteousness.”

27316.label: Acts 8:24
27316.text: In answer Simon said: “YOU men, make supplication for me to Jehovah that none of the things YOU have said may come upon me.”

27317.label: Acts 8:25
27317.text: Therefore, when they had given the witness thoroughly and had spoken the word of Jehovah, they turned back to Jerusalem, and they went declaring the good news to many villages of the Sa·marʹi·tans.

27318.label: Acts 8:26
27318.text: However, Jehovah’s angel spoke to Philip, saying: “Rise and go to the south to the road that runs down from Jerusalem to Gaʹza.” (This is a desert road.)

27319.label: Acts 8:27
27319.text: With that he rose and went, and, look! an E·thi·oʹpi·an eunuch, a man in power under Can·daʹce queen of the E·thi·oʹpi·ans, and who was over all her treasure. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,

27320.label: Acts 8:28
27320.text: but he was returning and was sitting in his chariot and reading aloud the prophet Isaiah.

27321.label: Acts 8:29
27321.text: So the spirit said to Philip: “Approach and join yourself to this chariot.”

27322.label: Acts 8:30
27322.text: Philip ran alongside and heard him reading aloud Isaiah the prophet, and he said: “Do you actually know what you are reading?”

27323.label: Acts 8:31
27323.text: He said: “Really, how could I ever do so, unless someone guided me?” And he entreated Philip to get on and sit down with him.

27324.label: Acts 8:32
27324.text: Now the passage of Scripture that he was reading aloud was this: “As a sheep he was brought to the slaughter, and as a lamb that is voiceless before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.

27325.label: Acts 8:33
27325.text: During his humiliation the judgment was taken away from him. Who will tell the details of his generation? Because his life is taken away from the earth.”

27326.label: Acts 8:34
27326.text: In answer the eunuch said to Philip: “I beg you, About whom does the prophet say this? About himself or about some other man?”

27327.label: Acts 8:35
27327.text: Philip opened his mouth and, starting with this Scripture, he declared to him the good news about Jesus.

27328.label: Acts 8:36
27328.text: Now as they were going over the road, they came to a certain body of water, and the eunuch said: “Look! A body of water; what prevents me from getting baptized?”

27330.label: Acts 8:38
27330.text: With that he commanded the chariot to halt, and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him.

27331.label: Acts 8:39
27331.text: When they had come up out of the water, Jehovah’s spirit quickly led Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him anymore, for he kept going on his way rejoicing.

27332.label: Acts 8:40
27332.text: But Philip was found to be in Ashʹdod, and he went through the territory and kept on declaring the good news to all the cities until he got to Caes·a·reʹa.

27333.label: Acts 9:1
27333.text: But Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest

27334.label: Acts 9:2
27334.text: and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, in order that he might bring bound to Jerusalem any whom he found who belonged to The Way, both men and women.

27335.label: Acts 9:3
27335.text: Now as he was traveling he approached Damascus, when suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him,

27336.label: Acts 9:4
27336.text: and he fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him: “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”

27337.label: Acts 9:5
27337.text: He said: “Who are you, Lord?” He said: “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

27338.label: Acts 9:6
27338.text: Nevertheless, rise and enter into the city, and what you must do will be told you.”

27339.label: Acts 9:7
27339.text: Now the men that were journeying with him were standing speechless, hearing, indeed, the sound of a voice, but not beholding any man.

27340.label: Acts 9:8
27340.text: But Saul got up from the ground, and though his eyes were opened he was seeing nothing. So they led him by the hand and conducted him into Damascus.

27341.label: Acts 9:9
27341.text: And for three days he did not see anything, and he neither ate nor drank.

27342.label: Acts 9:10
27342.text: There was in Damascus a certain disciple named An·a·niʹas, and the Lord said to him in a vision: “An·a·niʹas!” He said: “Here I am, Lord.”

27343.label: Acts 9:11
27343.text: The Lord said to him: “Rise, go to the street called Straight, and at the house of Judas look for a man named Saul, from Tarsus. For, look! he is praying,

27344.label: Acts 9:12
27344.text: and in a vision he has seen a man named An·a·niʹas come in and lay his hands upon him that he might recover sight.”

27345.label: Acts 9:13
27345.text: But An·a·niʹas answered: “Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how many injurious things he did to your holy ones in Jerusalem.

27346.label: Acts 9:14
27346.text: And here he has authority from the chief priests to put in bonds all those calling upon your name.”

27347.label: Acts 9:15
27347.text: But the Lord said to him: “Be on your way, because this man is a chosen vessel to me to bear my name to the nations as well as to kings and the sons of Israel.

27348.label: Acts 9:16
27348.text: For I shall show him plainly how many things he must suffer for my name.”

27349.label: Acts 9:17
27349.text: So An·a·niʹas went off and entered into the house, and he laid his hands upon him and said: “Saul, brother, the Lord, the Jesus that appeared to you on the road over which you were coming, has sent me forth, in order that you may recover sight and be filled with holy spirit.”

27350.label: Acts 9:18
27350.text: And immediately there fell from his eyes what looked like scales, and he recovered sight; and he rose and was baptized,

27351.label: Acts 9:19
27351.text: and he took food and gained strength. He got to be for some days with the disciples in Damascus,

27352.label: Acts 9:20
27352.text: and immediately in the synagogues he began to preach Jesus, that this One is the Son of God.

27353.label: Acts 9:21
27353.text: But all those hearing him gave way to astonishment and would say: “Is this not the man that ravaged those in Jerusalem who call upon this name, and that had come here for this very purpose, that he might lead them bound to the chief priests?”

27354.label: Acts 9:22
27354.text: But Saul kept on acquiring power all the more and was confounding the Jews that dwelt in Damascus as he proved logically that this is the Christ.

27355.label: Acts 9:23
27355.text: Now when a good many days were coming to a close, the Jews took counsel together to do away with him.

27356.label: Acts 9:24
27356.text: However, their plot against him became known to Saul. But they were closely watching also the gates both day and night in order to do away with him.

27357.label: Acts 9:25
27357.text: So his disciples took him and let him down by night through an opening in the wall, lowering him in a basket.

27358.label: Acts 9:26
27358.text: On arriving in Jerusalem he made efforts to join himself to the disciples; but they were all afraid of him, because they did not believe he was a disciple.

27359.label: Acts 9:27
27359.text: So Barʹna·bas came to his aid and led him to the apostles, and he told them in detail how on the road he had seen the Lord and that he had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.

27360.label: Acts 9:28
27360.text: And he continued with them, walking in and out at Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord;

27361.label: Acts 9:29
27361.text: and he was talking and disputing with the Greek-speaking Jews. But these made attempts to do away with him.

27362.label: Acts 9:30
27362.text: When the brothers detected this, they brought him down to Caes·a·reʹa and sent him off to Tarsus.

27363.label: Acts 9:31
27363.text: Then, indeed, the congregation throughout the whole of Ju·deʹa and Galʹi·lee and Sa·marʹi·a entered into a period of peace, being built up; and as it walked in the fear of Jehovah and in the comfort of the holy spirit it kept on multiplying.

27364.label: Acts 9:32
27364.text: Now as Peter was going through all [parts] he came down also to the holy ones that dwelt in Lydʹda.

27365.label: Acts 9:33
27365.text: There he found a certain man named Ae·neʹas, who had been lying flat on his cot for eight years, as he was paralyzed.

27366.label: Acts 9:34
27366.text: And Peter said to him: “Ae·neʹas, Jesus Christ heals you. Rise and make up your bed.” And he rose immediately.

27367.label: Acts 9:35
27367.text: And all those who inhabited Lydʹda and the [plain of] Sharʹon saw him, and these turned to the Lord.

27368.label: Acts 9:36
27368.text: But in Jopʹpa there was a certain disciple named Tabʹi·tha, which, when translated, means Dorʹcas. She abounded in good deeds and gifts of mercy that she was rendering.

27369.label: Acts 9:37
27369.text: But in those days she happened to fall sick and die. So they bathed her and laid her in an upper chamber.

27370.label: Acts 9:38
27370.text: Now as Lydʹda was near Jopʹpa, when the disciples heard that Peter was in this city they dispatched two men to him to entreat [him]: “Please do not hesitate to come on as far as us.”

27371.label: Acts 9:39
27371.text: At that Peter rose and went with them. And when he arrived, they led him up into the upper chamber; and all the widows presented themselves to him weeping and exhibiting many inner garments and outer garments that Dorʹcas used to make while she was with them.

27372.label: Acts 9:40
27372.text: But Peter put everybody outside and, bending his knees, he prayed, and, turning to the body, he said: “Tabʹi·tha, rise!” She opened her eyes and, as she caught sight of Peter, she sat up.

27373.label: Acts 9:41
27373.text: Giving her his hand, he raised her up, and he called the holy ones and the widows and presented her alive.

27374.label: Acts 9:42
27374.text: This became known throughout all Jopʹpa, and many became believers on the Lord.

27375.label: Acts 9:43
27375.text: For quite a few days he remained in Jopʹpa with a certain Simon, a tanner.

27376.label: Acts 10:1
27376.text: Now in Caes·a·reʹa there was a certain man named Cornelius, an army officer of the Italian band, as it was called,

27377.label: Acts 10:2
27377.text: a devout man and one fearing God together with all his household, and he made many gifts of mercy to the people and made supplication to God continually.

27378.label: Acts 10:3
27378.text: Just about the ninth hour of the day he saw plainly in a vision an angel of God come in to him and say to him: “Cornelius!”

27379.label: Acts 10:4
27379.text: The man gazed at him and, becoming frightened, said: “What is it, Lord?” He said to him: “Your prayers and gifts of mercy have ascended as a remembrance before God.

27380.label: Acts 10:5
27380.text: So now send men to Jopʹpa and summon a certain Simon who is surnamed Peter.

27381.label: Acts 10:6
27381.text: This man is being entertained by a certain Simon, a tanner, who has a house by the sea.”

27382.label: Acts 10:7
27382.text: As soon as the angel that spoke to him had left, he called two of his house servants and a devout soldier from among those who were in constant attendance upon him,

27383.label: Acts 10:8
27383.text: and he related everything to them and dispatched them to Jopʹpa.

27384.label: Acts 10:9
27384.text: The next day as they were pursuing their journey and were approaching the city, Peter went up to the housetop about the sixth hour to pray.

27385.label: Acts 10:10
27385.text: But he became very hungry and wanted to eat. While they were preparing, he fell into a trance

27386.label: Acts 10:11
27386.text: and beheld heaven opened and some sort of vessel descending like a great linen sheet being let down by its four extremities upon the earth;

27387.label: Acts 10:12
27387.text: and in it there were all sorts of four-footed creatures and creeping things of the earth and birds of heaven.

27388.label: Acts 10:13
27388.text: And a voice came to him: “Rise, Peter, slaughter and eat!”

27389.label: Acts 10:14
27389.text: But Peter said: “Not at all, Lord, because never have I eaten anything defiled and unclean.”

27390.label: Acts 10:15
27390.text: And the voice [spoke] again to him, the second time: “You stop calling defiled the things God has cleansed.”

27391.label: Acts 10:16
27391.text: This occurred a third time, and immediately the vessel was taken up into heaven.

27392.label: Acts 10:17
27392.text: Now while Peter was in great perplexity inwardly over what the vision he had seen might mean, look! the men dispatched by Cornelius had made inquiries for Simon’s house and stood there at the gate.

27393.label: Acts 10:18
27393.text: And they called out and inquired whether Simon who was surnamed Peter was being entertained there.

27394.label: Acts 10:19
27394.text: As Peter was going over in his mind about the vision, the spirit said: “Look! Three men are seeking you.

27395.label: Acts 10:20
27395.text: However, rise, go downstairs and be on your way with them, not doubting at all, because I have dispatched them.”

27396.label: Acts 10:21
27396.text: So Peter went downstairs to the men and said: “Look! I am the one YOU are seeking. What is the cause for which YOU are present?”

27397.label: Acts 10:22
27397.text: They said: “Cornelius, an army officer, a man righteous and fearing God and well reported by the whole nation of the Jews, was given divine instructions by a holy angel to send for you to come to his house and to hear the things you have to say.”

27398.label: Acts 10:23
27398.text: Therefore he invited them in and entertained them. The next day he rose and went off with them, and some of the brothers that were from Jopʹpa went with him.

27399.label: Acts 10:24
27399.text: On the day after that he entered into Caes·a·reʹa. Cornelius, of course, was expecting them and had called together his relatives and intimate friends.

27400.label: Acts 10:25
27400.text: As Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet and did obeisance to him.

27401.label: Acts 10:26
27401.text: But Peter lifted him up, saying: “Rise; I myself am also a man.”

27402.label: Acts 10:27
27402.text: And as he conversed with him he went in and found many people assembled,

27403.label: Acts 10:28
27403.text: and he said to them: “YOU well know how unlawful it is for a Jew to join himself to or approach a man of another race; and yet God has shown me I should call no man defiled or unclean.

27404.label: Acts 10:29
27404.text: Hence I came, really without objection, when I was sent for. Therefore I inquire the reason that YOU have sent for me.”

27405.label: Acts 10:30
27405.text: Accordingly Cornelius said: “Four days ago counting from this hour I was praying in my house at the ninth hour, when, look! a man in bright raiment stood before me

27406.label: Acts 10:31
27406.text: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been favorably heard and your gifts of mercy have been remembered before God.

27407.label: Acts 10:32
27407.text: Send, therefore, to Jopʹpa and call for Simon, who is surnamed Peter. This man is being entertained in the house of Simon, a tanner, by the sea.’

27408.label: Acts 10:33
27408.text: Therefore I at once sent to you, and you did well in coming here. And so at this time we are all present before God to hear all the things you have been commanded by Jehovah to say.”

27409.label: Acts 10:34
27409.text: At this Peter opened his mouth and said: “For a certainty I perceive that God is not partial,

27410.label: Acts 10:35
27410.text: but in every nation the man that fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.

27411.label: Acts 10:36
27411.text: He sent out the word to the sons of Israel to declare to them the good news of peace through Jesus Christ: this One is Lord of all [others].

27412.label: Acts 10:37
27412.text: YOU know the subject that was talked about throughout the whole of Ju·deʹa, starting from Galʹi·lee after the baptism that John preached,

27413.label: Acts 10:38
27413.text: namely, Jesus who was from Nazʹa·reth, how God anointed him with holy spirit and power, and he went through the land doing good and healing all those oppressed by the Devil; because God was with him.

27414.label: Acts 10:39
27414.text: And we are witnesses of all the things he did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem; but they also did away with him by hanging him on a stake.

27415.label: Acts 10:40
27415.text: God raised this One up on the third day and granted him to become manifest,

27416.label: Acts 10:41
27416.text: not to all the people, but to witnesses appointed beforehand by God, to us, who ate and drank with him after his rising from the dead.

27417.label: Acts 10:42
27417.text: Also, he ordered us to preach to the people and to give a thorough witness that this is the One decreed by God to be judge of the living and the dead.

27418.label: Acts 10:43
27418.text: To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone putting faith in him gets forgiveness of sins through his name.”

27419.label: Acts 10:44
27419.text: While Peter was yet speaking about these matters the holy spirit fell upon all those hearing the word.

27420.label: Acts 10:45
27420.text: And the faithful ones that had come with Peter who were of those circumcised were amazed, because the free gift of the holy spirit was being poured out also upon people of the nations.

27421.label: Acts 10:46
27421.text: For they heard them speaking with tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter responded:

27422.label: Acts 10:47
27422.text: “Can anyone forbid water so that these might not be baptized who have received the holy spirit even as we have?”

27423.label: Acts 10:48
27423.text: With that he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they requested him to remain for some days.

27424.label: Acts 11:1
27424.text: Now the apostles and the brothers that were in Ju·deʹa heard that people of the nations had also received the word of God.

27425.label: Acts 11:2
27425.text: So when Peter came up to Jerusalem, the [supporters] of circumcision began to contend with him,

27426.label: Acts 11:3
27426.text: saying he had gone into the house of men that were not circumcised and had eaten with them.

27427.label: Acts 11:4
27427.text: At this Peter commenced and went on to explain the particulars to them, saying:

27428.label: Acts 11:5
27428.text: “I was in the city of Jopʹpa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision, some sort of vessel descending like a great linen sheet being let down by its four extremities from heaven, and it came clear to me.

27429.label: Acts 11:6
27429.text: Gazing into it, I made observations and saw four-footed creatures of the earth and wild beasts and creeping things and birds of heaven.

27430.label: Acts 11:7
27430.text: I also heard a voice say to me, ‘Rise, Peter, slaughter and eat!’

27431.label: Acts 11:8
27431.text: But I said, ‘Not at all, Lord, because a defiled or unclean thing has never entered into my mouth.’

27432.label: Acts 11:9
27432.text: The second time the voice from heaven answered, ‘You stop calling defiled the things God has cleansed.’

27433.label: Acts 11:10
27433.text: This occurred for a third time, and everything was pulled up again into heaven.

27434.label: Acts 11:11
27434.text: Also, look! at that instant there were three men standing at the house in which we were, they having been dispatched from Caes·a·reʹa to me.

27435.label: Acts 11:12
27435.text: So the spirit told me to go with them, not doubting at all. But these six brothers also went with me, and we entered into the house of the man.

27436.label: Acts 11:13
27436.text: “He reported to us how he saw the angel stand in his house and say, ‘Dispatch men to Jopʹpa and send for Simon who is surnamed Peter,

27437.label: Acts 11:14
27437.text: and he will speak those things to you by which you and all your household may get saved.’

27438.label: Acts 11:15
27438.text: But when I started to speak, the holy spirit fell upon them just as it did also upon us in [the] beginning.

27439.label: Acts 11:16
27439.text: At this I called to mind the saying of the Lord, how he used to say, ‘John, for his part, baptized with water, but YOU will be baptized in holy spirit.’

27440.label: Acts 11:17
27440.text: If, therefore, God gave the same free gift to them as he also did to us who have believed upon the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I should be able to hinder God?”

27441.label: Acts 11:18
27441.text: Now when they heard these things, they acquiesced, and they glorified God, saying: “Well, then, God has granted repentance for the purpose of life to people of the nations also.”

27442.label: Acts 11:19
27442.text: Consequently those who had been scattered by the tribulation that arose over Stephen went through as far as Phoe·niʹcia and Cyʹprus and Antioch, but speaking the word to no one except to Jews only.

27443.label: Acts 11:20
27443.text: However, out of them there were some men of Cyʹprus and Cy·reʹne that came to Antioch and began talking to the Greek-speaking people, declaring the good news of the Lord Jesus.

27444.label: Acts 11:21
27444.text: Furthermore, the hand of Jehovah was with them, and a great number that became believers turned to the Lord.

27445.label: Acts 11:22
27445.text: The account about them got to the ears of the congregation that was in Jerusalem, and they sent out Barʹna·bas as far as Antioch.

27446.label: Acts 11:23
27446.text: When he arrived and saw the undeserved kindness of God, he rejoiced and began to encourage them all to continue in the Lord with hearty purpose;

27447.label: Acts 11:24
27447.text: for he was a good man and full of holy spirit and of faith. And a considerable crowd was added to the Lord.

27448.label: Acts 11:25
27448.text: So he went off to Tarsus to make a thorough search for Saul

27449.label: Acts 11:26
27449.text: and, after he found him, he brought him to Antioch. It thus came about that for a whole year they gathered together with them in the congregation and taught quite a crowd, and it was first in Antioch that the disciples were by divine providence called Christians.

27450.label: Acts 11:27
27450.text: Now in these days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

27451.label: Acts 11:28
27451.text: One of them named Agʹa·bus rose and proceeded to indicate through the spirit that a great famine was about to come upon the entire inhabited earth; which, for that matter, did take place in the time of Claudius.

27452.label: Acts 11:29
27452.text: So those of the disciples determined, each of them according as anyone could afford it, to send a relief ministration to the brothers dwelling in Ju·deʹa;

27453.label: Acts 11:30
27453.text: and this they did, dispatching it to the older men by the hand of Barʹna·bas and Saul.

27454.label: Acts 12:1
27454.text: About that particular time Herod the king applied his hands to mistreating some of those of the congregation.

27455.label: Acts 12:2
27455.text: He did away with James the brother of John by the sword.

27456.label: Acts 12:3
27456.text: As he saw it was pleasing to the Jews, he went on to arrest Peter also. (As it was, those were days of the unfermented cakes.)

27457.label: Acts 12:4
27457.text: And laying hold of him, he put him in prison, turning him over to four shifts of four soldiers each to guard him, as he intended to produce him for the people after the passover.

27458.label: Acts 12:5
27458.text: Consequently Peter was being kept in the prison; but prayer to God for him was being carried on intensely by the congregation.

27459.label: Acts 12:6
27459.text: Now when Herod was about to produce him, that night Peter was sleeping bound with two chains between two soldiers, and guards before the door were keeping the prison.

27460.label: Acts 12:7
27460.text: But, look! Jehovah’s angel stood by, and a light shone in the prison cell. Striking Peter on the side, he roused him, saying: “Rise quickly!” And his chains fell off his hands.

27461.label: Acts 12:8
27461.text: The angel said to him: “Gird yourself and bind your sandals on.” He did so. Finally he said to him: “Put your outer garment on and keep following me.”

27462.label: Acts 12:9
27462.text: And he went out and kept following him, but he did not know that what was happening through the angel was real. In fact, he supposed he was seeing a vision.

27463.label: Acts 12:10
27463.text: Going through the first sentinel guard and the second they got to the iron gate leading into the city, and this opened to them of its own accord. And after they went out they advanced down one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.

27464.label: Acts 12:11
27464.text: And Peter, coming to himself, said: “Now I actually know that Jehovah sent his angel forth and delivered me out of Herod’s hand and from all that the people of the Jews were expecting.”

27465.label: Acts 12:12
27465.text: And after he considered it, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John who was surnamed Mark, where quite a few were gathered together and praying.

27466.label: Acts 12:13
27466.text: When he knocked at the door of the gateway, a servant girl named Rhoda came to attend to the call,

27467.label: Acts 12:14
27467.text: and, upon recognizing the voice of Peter, out of joy she did not open the gate, but ran inside and reported that Peter was standing before the gateway.

27468.label: Acts 12:15
27468.text: They said to her: “You are mad.” But she kept on strongly asserting it was so. They began to say: “It is his angel.”

27469.label: Acts 12:16
27469.text: But Peter remained there knocking. When they opened, they saw him and were astonished.

27470.label: Acts 12:17
27470.text: But he motioned to them with his hand to be silent and told them in detail how Jehovah brought him out of the prison, and he said: “Report these things to James and the brothers.” With that he went out and journeyed to another place.

27471.label: Acts 12:18
27471.text: Well, when it became day, there was no little stir among the soldiers over what really had become of Peter.

27472.label: Acts 12:19
27472.text: Herod made diligent search for him and, when not finding him, he examined the guards and commanded them to be led off [to punishment]; and he went down from Ju·deʹa to Caes·a·reʹa and spent some time there.

27473.label: Acts 12:20
27473.text: Now he was in a fighting mood against the people of Tyre and of Siʹdon. So with one accord they came to him and, after persuading Blastus, who was in charge of the bedchamber of the king, they began suing for peace, because their country was supplied with food from that of the king.

27474.label: Acts 12:21
27474.text: But on a set day Herod clothed himself with royal raiment and sat down upon the judgment seat and began giving them a public address.

27475.label: Acts 12:22
27475.text: In turn the assembled people began shouting: “A god’s voice, and not a man’s!”

27476.label: Acts 12:23
27476.text: Instantly the angel of Jehovah struck him, because he did not give the glory to God; and he became eaten up with worms and expired.

27477.label: Acts 12:24
27477.text: But the word of Jehovah went on growing and spreading.

27478.label: Acts 12:25
27478.text: As for Barʹna·bas and Saul, after having fully carried out the relief ministration in Jerusalem, they returned and took along with them John, the one surnamed Mark.

27479.label: Acts 13:1
27479.text: Now in Antioch there were prophets and teachers in the local congregation, Barʹna·bas as well as Symʹe·on who was called Niʹger, and Lucius of Cy·reʹne, and Manʹa·en who was educated with Herod the district ruler, and Saul.

27480.label: Acts 13:2
27480.text: As they were publicly ministering to Jehovah and fasting, the holy spirit said: “Of all persons set Barʹna·bas and Saul apart for me for the work to which I have called them.”

27481.label: Acts 13:3
27481.text: Then they fasted and prayed and laid their hands upon them and let them go.

27482.label: Acts 13:4
27482.text: Accordingly these men, sent out by the holy spirit, went down to Se·leuʹcia, and from there they sailed away to Cyʹprus.

27483.label: Acts 13:5
27483.text: And when they got to be in Salʹa·mis they began publishing the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. They had John also as an attendant.

27484.label: Acts 13:6
27484.text: When they had gone through the whole island as far as Paʹphos, they met up with a certain man, a sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew whose name was Bar-Jeʹsus,

27485.label: Acts 13:7
27485.text: and he was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. Calling Barʹna·bas and Saul to him, this man earnestly sought to hear the word of God.

27486.label: Acts 13:8
27486.text: But Elʹy·mas the sorcerer (that, in fact, is the way his name is translated) began opposing them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

27487.label: Acts 13:9
27487.text: Saul, who is also Paul, becoming filled with holy spirit, looked at him intently

27488.label: Acts 13:10
27488.text: and said: “O man full of every sort of fraud and every sort of villainy, you son of the Devil, you enemy of everything righteous, will you not quit distorting the right ways of Jehovah?

27489.label: Acts 13:11
27489.text: Well, then, look! Jehovah’s hand is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sunlight for a period of time.” Instantly a thick mist and darkness fell upon him, and he went around seeking men to lead him by the hand.

27490.label: Acts 13:12
27490.text: Then the proconsul, upon seeing what had happened, became a believer, as he was astounded at the teaching of Jehovah.

27491.label: Acts 13:13
27491.text: The men, together with Paul, now put out to sea from Paʹphos and arrived at Perga in Pam·phylʹi·a. But John withdrew from them and returned to Jerusalem.

27492.label: Acts 13:14
27492.text: They, however, went on from Perga and came to Antioch in Pi·sidʹi·a and, going into the synagogue on the sabbath day, they took a seat.

27493.label: Acts 13:15
27493.text: After the public reading of the Law and of the Prophets the presiding officers of the synagogue sent out to them, saying: “Men, brothers, if there is any word of encouragement for the people that YOU have, tell it.”

27494.label: Acts 13:16
27494.text: So Paul rose, and motioning with his hand, he said: “Men, Israelites and YOU [others] that fear God, hear.

27495.label: Acts 13:17
27495.text: The God of this people Israel chose our forefathers, and he exalted the people during their alien residence in the land of Egypt and brought them out of it with an uplifted arm.

27496.label: Acts 13:18
27496.text: And for a period of about forty years he put up with their manner of action in the wilderness.

27497.label: Acts 13:19
27497.text: After destroying seven nations in the land of Caʹnaan, he distributed the land of them by lot:

27498.label: Acts 13:20
27498.text: all that during about four hundred and fifty years. “And after these things he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.

27499.label: Acts 13:21
27499.text: But from then on they demanded a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

27500.label: Acts 13:22
27500.text: And after removing him, he raised up for them David as king, respecting whom he bore witness and said, ‘I have found David the son of Jesʹse, a man agreeable to my heart, who will do all the things I desire.’

27501.label: Acts 13:23
27501.text: From the offspring of this [man] according to his promise God has brought to Israel a savior, Jesus,

27502.label: Acts 13:24
27502.text: after John, in advance of the entry of that One, had preached publicly to all the people of Israel baptism [in symbol] of repentance.

27503.label: Acts 13:25
27503.text: But as John was fulfilling his course, he would say, ‘What do YOU suppose I am? I am not he. But, look! one is coming after me the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.’

27504.label: Acts 13:26
27504.text: “Men, brothers, YOU sons of the stock of Abraham and those [others] among YOU who fear God, the word of this salvation has been sent forth to us.

27505.label: Acts 13:27
27505.text: For the inhabitants of Jerusalem and their rulers did not know this One, but, when acting as judges, they fulfilled the things voiced by the Prophets, which things are read aloud every Sabbath,

27506.label: Acts 13:28
27506.text: and, although they found no cause for death, they demanded of Pilate that he be executed.

27507.label: Acts 13:29
