27507.text: When, now, they had accomplished all the things written about him, they took him down from the stake and laid him in a memorial tomb.

27508.label: Acts 13:30
27508.text: But God raised him up from the dead;

27509.label: Acts 13:31
27509.text: and for many days he became visible to those who had gone up with him from Galʹi·lee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses to the people.

27510.label: Acts 13:32
27510.text: “And so we are declaring to YOU the good news about the promise made to the forefathers,

27511.label: Acts 13:33
27511.text: that God has entirely fulfilled it to us their children in that he resurrected Jesus; even as it is written in the second psalm, ‘You are my son, I have become your Father this day.’

27512.label: Acts 13:34
27512.text: And that fact that he resurrected him from the dead destined no more to return to corruption, he has stated in this way, ‘I will give YOU people the loving-kindnesses to David that are faithful.’

27513.label: Acts 13:35
27513.text: Hence he also says in another psalm, ‘You will not allow your loyal one to see corruption.’

27514.label: Acts 13:36
27514.text: For David, on the one hand, served the express will of God in his own generation and fell asleep [in death] and was laid with his forefathers and did see corruption.

27515.label: Acts 13:37
27515.text: On the other hand, he whom God raised up did not see corruption.

27516.label: Acts 13:38
27516.text: “Let it therefore be known to YOU, brothers, that through this One a forgiveness of sins is being published to YOU;

27517.label: Acts 13:39
27517.text: and that from all the things from which YOU could not be declared guiltless by means of the law of Moses, everyone who believes is declared guiltless by means of this One.

27518.label: Acts 13:40
27518.text: Therefore see to it that what is said in the Prophets does not come upon YOU,

27519.label: Acts 13:41
27519.text: ‘Behold it, YOU scorners, and wonder at it, and vanish away, because I am working a work in YOUR days, a work that YOU will by no means believe even if anyone relates it to YOU in detail.’”

27520.label: Acts 13:42
27520.text: Now when they were going out, the people began entreating for these matters to be spoken to them on the following sabbath.

27521.label: Acts 13:43
27521.text: So after the synagogue assembly was dissolved, many of the Jews and of the proselytes who worshiped [God] followed Paul and Barʹna·bas, who in speaking to them began urging them to continue in the undeserved kindness of God.

27522.label: Acts 13:44
27522.text: The next sabbath nearly all the city gathered together to hear the word of Jehovah.

27523.label: Acts 13:45
27523.text: When the Jews got sight of the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and began blasphemously contradicting the things being spoken by Paul.

27524.label: Acts 13:46
27524.text: And so, talking with boldness, Paul and Barʹna·bas said: “It was necessary for the word of God to be spoken first to YOU. Since YOU are thrusting it away from YOU and do not judge yourselves worthy of everlasting life, look! we turn to the nations.

27525.label: Acts 13:47
27525.text: In fact, Jehovah has laid commandment upon us in these words, ‘I have appointed you as a light of nations, for you to be a salvation to the extremity of the earth.’”

27526.label: Acts 13:48
27526.text: When those of the nations heard this, they began to rejoice and to glorify the word of Jehovah, and all those who were rightly disposed for everlasting life became believers.

27527.label: Acts 13:49
27527.text: Furthermore, the word of Jehovah went on being carried throughout the whole country.

27528.label: Acts 13:50
27528.text: But the Jews stirred up the reputable women who worshiped [God] and the principal men of the city, and they raised up a persecution against Paul and Barʹna·bas and threw them outside their boundaries.

27529.label: Acts 13:51
27529.text: These shook the dust off their feet against them and went to I·coʹni·um.

27530.label: Acts 13:52
27530.text: And the disciples continued to be filled with joy and holy spirit.

27531.label: Acts 14:1
27531.text: Now in I·coʹni·um they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke in such a manner that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks became believers.

27532.label: Acts 14:2
27532.text: But the Jews that did not believe stirred up and wrongly influenced the souls of people of the nations against the brothers.

27533.label: Acts 14:3
27533.text: Therefore they spent considerable time speaking with boldness by the authority of Jehovah, who bore witness to the word of his undeserved kindness by granting signs and portents to occur through their hands.

27534.label: Acts 14:4
27534.text: However, the multitude of the city was split, and some were for the Jews but others for the apostles.

27535.label: Acts 14:5
27535.text: Now when a violent attempt took place on the part of both people of the nations and Jews with their rulers, to treat them insolently and pelt them with stones,

27536.label: Acts 14:6
27536.text: they, on being informed of it, fled to the cities of Lyc·a·oʹni·a, Lysʹtra and Derʹbe and the country round about;

27537.label: Acts 14:7
27537.text: and there they went on declaring the good news.

27538.label: Acts 14:8
27538.text: Now in Lysʹtra there was sitting a certain man disabled in his feet, lame from his mother’s womb, and he had never walked at all.

27539.label: Acts 14:9
27539.text: This man was listening to Paul speak, who, on looking at him intently and seeing he had faith to be made well,

27540.label: Acts 14:10
27540.text: said with a loud voice: “Stand up erect on your feet.” And he leaped up and began walking.

27541.label: Acts 14:11
27541.text: And the crowds, seeing what Paul had done, raised their voices, saying in the Lyc·a·oʹni·an tongue: “The gods have become like humans and have come down to us!”

27542.label: Acts 14:12
27542.text: And they went calling Barʹna·bas Zeus, but Paul Herʹmes, since he was the one taking the lead in speaking.

27543.label: Acts 14:13
27543.text: And the priest of Zeus, whose [temple] was before the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates and was desiring to offer sacrifices with the crowds.

27544.label: Acts 14:14
27544.text: However, when the apostles Barʹna·bas and Paul heard of it, they ripped their outer garments and leaped out into the crowd, crying out

27545.label: Acts 14:15
27545.text: and saying: “Men, why are YOU doing these things? We also are humans having the same infirmities as YOU do, and are declaring the good news to YOU, for YOU to turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things in them.

27546.label: Acts 14:16
27546.text: In the past generations he permitted all the nations to go on in their ways,

27547.label: Acts 14:17
27547.text: although, indeed, he did not leave himself without witness in that he did good, giving YOU rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling YOUR hearts to the full with food and good cheer.”

27548.label: Acts 14:18
27548.text: And yet by saying these things they scarcely restrained the crowds from sacrificing to them.

27549.label: Acts 14:19
27549.text: But Jews arrived from Antioch and I·coʹni·um and persuaded the crowds, and they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, imagining he was dead.

27550.label: Acts 14:20
27550.text: However, when the disciples surrounded him, he rose up and entered into the city. And on the next day he left with Barʹna·bas for Derʹbe.

27551.label: Acts 14:21
27551.text: And after declaring the good news to that city and making quite a few disciples, they returned to Lysʹtra and to I·coʹni·um and to Antioch,

27552.label: Acts 14:22
27552.text: strengthening the souls of the disciples, encouraging them to remain in the faith and [saying]: “We must enter into the kingdom of God through many tribulations.”

27553.label: Acts 14:23
27553.text: Moreover, they appointed older men for them in each congregation and, offering prayer with fastings, they committed them to Jehovah in whom they had become believers.

27554.label: Acts 14:24
27554.text: And they went through Pi·sidʹi·a and came into Pam·phylʹi·a,

27555.label: Acts 14:25
27555.text: and, after speaking the word in Perga, they went down to At·ta·liʹa.

27556.label: Acts 14:26
27556.text: And from there they sailed off for Antioch, where they had been entrusted to the undeserved kindness of God for the work they had fully performed.

27557.label: Acts 14:27
27557.text: When they had arrived and had gathered the congregation together, they proceeded to relate the many things God had done by means of them, and that he had opened to the nations the door to faith.

27558.label: Acts 14:28
27558.text: So they spent not a little time with the disciples.

27559.label: Acts 15:1
27559.text: And certain men came down from Ju·deʹa and began to teach the brothers: “Unless YOU get circumcised according to the custom of Moses, YOU cannot be saved.”

27560.label: Acts 15:2
27560.text: But when there had occurred no little dissension and disputing by Paul and Barʹna·bas with them, they arranged for Paul and Barʹna·bas and some others of them to go up to the apostles and older men in Jerusalem regarding this dispute.

27561.label: Acts 15:3
27561.text: Accordingly, after being conducted partway by the congregation, these men continued on their way through both Phoe·niʹcia and Sa·marʹi·a, relating in detail the conversion of people of the nations, and they were causing great joy to all the brothers.

27562.label: Acts 15:4
27562.text: On arriving in Jerusalem they were kindly received by the congregation and the apostles and the older men, and they recounted the many things God had done by means of them.

27563.label: Acts 15:5
27563.text: Yet, some of those of the sect of the Pharisees that had believed rose up from their seats and said: “It is necessary to circumcise them and charge them to observe the law of Moses.”

27564.label: Acts 15:6
27564.text: And the apostles and the older men gathered together to see about this affair.

27565.label: Acts 15:7
27565.text: Now when much disputing had taken place, Peter rose and said to them: “Men, brothers, YOU well know that from early days God made the choice among YOU that through my mouth people of the nations should hear the word of the good news and believe;

27566.label: Acts 15:8
27566.text: and God, who knows the heart, bore witness by giving them the holy spirit, just as he did to us also.

27567.label: Acts 15:9
27567.text: And he made no distinction at all between us and them, but purified their hearts by faith.

27568.label: Acts 15:10
27568.text: Now, therefore, why are YOU making a test of God by imposing upon the neck of the disciples a yoke that neither our forefathers nor we were capable of bearing?

27569.label: Acts 15:11
27569.text: On the contrary, we trust to get saved through the undeserved kindness of the Lord Jesus in the same way as those people also.”

27570.label: Acts 15:12
27570.text: At that the entire multitude became silent, and they began to listen to Barʹna·bas and Paul relate the many signs and portents that God did through them among the nations.

27571.label: Acts 15:13
27571.text: After they quit speaking, James answered, saying: “Men, brothers, hear me.

27572.label: Acts 15:14
27572.text: Symʹe·on has related thoroughly how God for the first time turned his attention to the nations to take out of them a people for his name.

27573.label: Acts 15:15
27573.text: And with this the words of the Prophets agree, just as it is written,

27574.label: Acts 15:16
27574.text: ‘After these things I shall return and rebuild the booth of David that is fallen down; and I shall rebuild its ruins and erect it again,

27575.label: Acts 15:17
27575.text: in order that those who remain of the men may earnestly seek Jehovah, together with people of all the nations, people who are called by my name, says Jehovah, who is doing these things,

27577.label: Acts 15:19
27577.text: Hence my decision is not to trouble those from the nations who are turning to God,

27578.label: Acts 15:20
27578.text: but to write them to abstain from things polluted by idols and from fornication and from what is strangled and from blood.

27579.label: Acts 15:21
27579.text: For from ancient times Moses has had in city after city those who preach him, because he is read aloud in the synagogues on every sabbath.”

27580.label: Acts 15:22
27580.text: Then the apostles and the older men together with the whole congregation favored sending chosen men from among them to Antioch along with Paul and Barʹna·bas, namely, Judas who was called Barʹsab·bas and Silas, leading men among the brothers;

27581.label: Acts 15:23
27581.text: and by their hand they wrote: “The apostles and the older men, brothers, to those brothers in Antioch and Syria and Ci·liʹcia who are from the nations: Greetings!

27582.label: Acts 15:24
27582.text: Since we have heard that some from among us have caused YOU trouble with speeches, trying to subvert YOUR souls, although we did not give them any instructions,

27583.label: Acts 15:25
27583.text: we have come to a unanimous accord and have favored choosing men to send to YOU together with our loved ones, Barʹna·bas and Paul,

27584.label: Acts 15:26
27584.text: men that have delivered up their souls for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

27585.label: Acts 15:27
27585.text: We are therefore dispatching Judas and Silas, that they also may report the same things by word.

27586.label: Acts 15:28
27586.text: For the holy spirit and we ourselves have favored adding no further burden to YOU, except these necessary things,

27587.label: Acts 15:29
27587.text: to keep abstaining from things sacrificed to idols and from blood and from things strangled and from fornication. If YOU carefully keep yourselves from these things, YOU will prosper. Good health to YOU!”

27588.label: Acts 15:30
27588.text: Accordingly, when these men were let go, they went down to Antioch, and they gathered the multitude together and handed them the letter.

27589.label: Acts 15:31
27589.text: After reading it, they rejoiced over the encouragement.

27590.label: Acts 15:32
27590.text: And Judas and Silas, since they themselves were also prophets, encouraged the brothers with many a discourse and strengthened them.

27591.label: Acts 15:33
27591.text: So, when they had passed some time, they were let go in peace by the brothers to those who had sent them out.

27593.label: Acts 15:35
27593.text: However, Paul and Barʹna·bas continued spending time in Antioch teaching and declaring, with many others also, the good news of the word of Jehovah.

27594.label: Acts 15:36
27594.text: Now after some days Paul said to Barʹna·bas: “Above all things, let us return and visit the brothers in every one of the cities in which we published the word of Jehovah to see how they are.”

27595.label: Acts 15:37
27595.text: For his part, Barʹna·bas was determined to take along also John, who was called Mark.

27596.label: Acts 15:38
27596.text: But Paul did not think it proper to be taking this one along with them, seeing that he had departed from them from Pam·phylʹi·a and had not gone with them to the work.

27597.label: Acts 15:39
27597.text: At this there occurred a sharp burst of anger, so that they separated from each other; and Barʹna·bas took Mark along and sailed away to Cyʹprus.

27598.label: Acts 15:40
27598.text: Paul selected Silas and went off after he had been entrusted by the brothers to the undeserved kindness of Jehovah.

27599.label: Acts 15:41
27599.text: But he went through Syria and Ci·liʹcia, strengthening the congregations.

27600.label: Acts 16:1
27600.text: So he arrived at Derʹbe and also at Lysʹtra. And, look! a certain disciple was there by the name of Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman but of a Greek father,

27601.label: Acts 16:2
27601.text: and he was well reported on by the brothers in Lysʹtra and I·coʹni·um.

27602.label: Acts 16:3
27602.text: Paul expressed the desire for this man to go out with him, and he took him and circumcised him because of the Jews that were in those places, for one and all knew that his father was a Greek.

27603.label: Acts 16:4
27603.text: Now as they traveled on through the cities they would deliver to those there for observance the decrees that had been decided upon by the apostles and older men who were in Jerusalem.

27604.label: Acts 16:5
27604.text: Therefore, indeed, the congregations continued to be made firm in the faith and to increase in number from day to day.

27605.label: Acts 16:6
27605.text: Moreover, they went through Phrygʹi·a and the country of Ga·laʹti·a, because they were forbidden by the holy spirit to speak the word in the [district of] Asia.

27606.label: Acts 16:7
27606.text: Further, when getting down to Mysʹi·a they made efforts to go into Bi·thynʹi·a, but the spirit of Jesus did not permit them.

27607.label: Acts 16:8
27607.text: So they passed Mysʹi·a by and came down to Troʹas.

27608.label: Acts 16:9
27608.text: And during the night a vision appeared to Paul: a certain Mac·e·doʹni·an man was standing and entreating him and saying: “Step over into Mac·e·doʹni·a and help us.”

27609.label: Acts 16:10
27609.text: Now as soon as he had seen the vision, we sought to go forth into Mac·e·doʹni·a, drawing the conclusion that God had summoned us to declare the good news to them.

27610.label: Acts 16:11
27610.text: Therefore we put out to sea from Troʹas and came with a straight run to Samʹo·thrace, but on the following day to Ne·apʹo·lis,

27611.label: Acts 16:12
27611.text: and from there to Phi·lipʹpi, a colony, which is the principal city of the district of Mac·e·doʹni·a. We continued in this city, spending some days.

27612.label: Acts 16:13
27612.text: And on the sabbath day we went forth outside the gate beside a river, where we were thinking there was a place of prayer; and we sat down and began speaking to the women that had assembled.

27613.label: Acts 16:14
27613.text: And a certain woman named Lydʹi·a, a seller of purple, of the city of Thy·a·tiʹra and a worshiper of God, was listening, and Jehovah opened her heart wide to pay attention to the things being spoken by Paul.

27614.label: Acts 16:15
27614.text: Now when she and her household got baptized, she said with entreaty: “If YOU men have judged me to be faithful to Jehovah, enter into my house and stay.” And she just made us come.

27615.label: Acts 16:16
27615.text: And it happened that as we were going to the place of prayer, a certain servant girl with a spirit, a demon of divination, met us. She used to furnish her masters with much gain by practicing the art of prediction.

27616.label: Acts 16:17
27616.text: This [girl] kept following Paul and us and crying out with the words: “These men are slaves of the Most High God, who are publishing to YOU the way of salvation.”

27617.label: Acts 16:18
27617.text: This she kept doing for many days. Finally Paul got tired of it and turned and said to the spirit: “I order you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her.” And it came out that very hour.

27618.label: Acts 16:19
27618.text: Well, when her masters saw that their hope of gain had left, they laid hold of Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace to the rulers,

27619.label: Acts 16:20
27619.text: and, leading them up to the civil magistrates, they said: “These men are disturbing our city very much, they being Jews,

27620.label: Acts 16:21
27620.text: and they are publishing customs that it is not lawful for us to take up or practice, seeing we are Romans.”

27621.label: Acts 16:22
27621.text: And the crowd rose up together against them; and the civil magistrates, after tearing the outer garments off them, gave the command to beat them with rods.

27622.label: Acts 16:23
27622.text: After they had inflicted many blows upon them, they threw them into prison, ordering the jailer to keep them securely.

27623.label: Acts 16:24
27623.text: Because he got such an order, he threw them into the inner prison and made their feet fast in the stocks.

27624.label: Acts 16:25
27624.text: But about the middle of the night Paul and Silas were praying and praising God with song; yes, the prisoners were hearing them.

27625.label: Acts 16:26
27625.text: Suddenly a great earthquake occurred, so that the foundations of the jail were shaken. Moreover, all the doors were instantly opened, and the bonds of all were loosened.

27626.label: Acts 16:27
27626.text: The jailer, being awakened out of sleep and seeing the prison doors were open, drew his sword and was about to do away with himself, imagining that the prisoners had escaped.

27627.label: Acts 16:28
27627.text: But Paul called out with a loud voice, saying: “Do not hurt yourself, for we are all here!”

27628.label: Acts 16:29
27628.text: So he asked for lights and leaped in and, seized with trembling, he fell down before Paul and Silas.

27629.label: Acts 16:30
27629.text: And he brought them outside and said: “Sirs, what must I do to get saved?”

27630.label: Acts 16:31
27630.text: They said: “Believe on the Lord Jesus and you will get saved, you and your household.”

27631.label: Acts 16:32
27631.text: And they spoke the word of Jehovah to him together with all those in his house.

27632.label: Acts 16:33
27632.text: And he took them along in that hour of the night and bathed their stripes; and, one and all, he and his were baptized without delay.

27633.label: Acts 16:34
27633.text: And he brought them into his house and set a table before them, and he rejoiced greatly with all his household now that he had believed God.

27634.label: Acts 16:35
27634.text: When it became day, the civil magistrates dispatched the constables to say: “Release those men.”

27635.label: Acts 16:36
27635.text: So the jailer reported their words to Paul: “The civil magistrates have dispatched men that YOU [two] might be released. Now, therefore, come out and go YOUR way in peace.”

27636.label: Acts 16:37
27636.text: But Paul said to them: “They flogged us publicly uncondemned, men who are Romans, and threw us into prison; and are they now throwing us out secretly? No, indeed! but let them come themselves and bring us out.”

27637.label: Acts 16:38
27637.text: So the constables reported these sayings to the civil magistrates. These grew fearful when they heard that the men were Romans.

27638.label: Acts 16:39
27638.text: Consequently they came and entreated them and, after bringing them out, they requested them to depart from the city.

27639.label: Acts 16:40
27639.text: But they came out of the prison and went to the home of Lydʹi·a, and when they saw the brothers they encouraged them and departed.

27640.label: Acts 17:1
27640.text: They now journeyed through Am·phipʹo·lis and Ap·ol·loʹni·a and came to Thes·sa·lo·niʹca, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.

27641.label: Acts 17:2
27641.text: So according to Paul’s custom he went inside to them, and for three sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

27642.label: Acts 17:3
27642.text: explaining and proving by references that it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead, and [saying]: “This is the Christ, this Jesus whom I am publishing to YOU.”

27643.label: Acts 17:4
27643.text: As a result some of them became believers and associated themselves with Paul and Silas, and a great multitude of the Greeks who worshiped [God] and not a few of the principal women did so.

27644.label: Acts 17:5
27644.text: But the Jews, getting jealous, took into their company certain wicked men of the marketplace idlers and formed a mob and proceeded to throw the city into an uproar. And they assaulted the house of Jaʹson and went seeking to have them brought forth to the rabble.

27645.label: Acts 17:6
27645.text: When they did not find them they dragged Jaʹson and certain brothers to the city rulers, crying out: “These men that have overturned the inhabited earth are present here also,

27646.label: Acts 17:7
27646.text: and Jaʹson has received them with hospitality. And all these [men] act in opposition to the decrees of Caesar, saying there is another king, Jesus.”

27647.label: Acts 17:8
27647.text: They indeed agitated the crowd and the city rulers when they heard these things;

27648.label: Acts 17:9
27648.text: and first after taking sufficient security from Jaʹson and the others they let them go.

27649.label: Acts 17:10
27649.text: Immediately by night the brothers sent both Paul and Silas out to Be·roeʹa, and these, upon arriving, went into the synagogue of the Jews.

27650.label: Acts 17:11
27650.text: Now the latter were more noble-minded than those in Thes·sa·lo·niʹca, for they received the word with the greatest eagerness of mind, carefully examining the Scriptures daily as to whether these things were so.

27651.label: Acts 17:12
27651.text: Therefore many of them became believers, and so did not a few of the reputable Greek women and of the men.

27652.label: Acts 17:13
27652.text: But when the Jews from Thes·sa·lo·niʹca learned that the word of God was published also in Be·roeʹa by Paul, they came there also to incite and agitate the masses.

27653.label: Acts 17:14
27653.text: Then the brothers immediately sent Paul off to go as far as the sea; but both Silas and Timothy remained behind there.

27654.label: Acts 17:15
27654.text: However, those conducting Paul brought him as far as Athens and, after receiving a command for Silas and Timothy to come to him as quickly as possible, they departed.

27655.label: Acts 17:16
27655.text: Now while Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit within him came to be irritated at beholding that the city was full of idols.

27656.label: Acts 17:17
27656.text: Consequently he began to reason in the synagogue with the Jews and the other people who worshiped [God] and every day in the marketplace with those who happened to be on hand.

27657.label: Acts 17:18
27657.text: But certain ones of both the Ep·i·cu·reʹan and the Stoʹic philosophers took to conversing with him controversially, and some would say: “What is it this chatterer would like to tell?” Others: “He seems to be a publisher of foreign deities.” This was because he was declaring the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.

27658.label: Acts 17:19
27658.text: So they laid hold of him and led him to the Ar·e·opʹa·gus, saying: “Can we get to know what this new teaching is which is spoken by you?

27659.label: Acts 17:20
27659.text: For you are introducing some things that are strange to our ears. Therefore we desire to get to know what these things purport to be.”

27660.label: Acts 17:21
27660.text: In fact, all Athenians and the foreigners sojourning there would spend their leisure time at nothing but telling something or listening to something new.

27661.label: Acts 17:22
27661.text: Paul now stood in the midst of the Ar·e·opʹa·gus and said: “Men of Athens, I behold that in all things YOU seem to be more given to the fear of the deities than others are.

27662.label: Acts 17:23
27662.text: For instance, while passing along and carefully observing YOUR objects of veneration I also found an altar on which had been inscribed ‘To an Unknown God.’ Therefore what YOU are unknowingly giving godly devotion to, this I am publishing to YOU.

27663.label: Acts 17:24
27663.text: The God that made the world and all the things in it, being, as this One is, Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in handmade temples,

27664.label: Acts 17:25
27664.text: neither is he attended to by human hands as if he needed anything, because he himself gives to all [persons] life and breath and all things.

27665.label: Acts 17:26
27665.text: And he made out of one [man] every nation of men, to dwell upon the entire surface of the earth, and he decreed the appointed times and the set limits of the dwelling of [men],

27666.label: Acts 17:27
27666.text: for them to seek God, if they might grope for him and really find him, although, in fact, he is not far off from each one of us.

27667.label: Acts 17:28
27667.text: For by him we have life and move and exist, even as certain ones of the poets among YOU have said, ‘For we are also his progeny.’

27668.label: Acts 17:29
27668.text: “Seeing, therefore, that we are the progeny of God, we ought not to imagine that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, like something sculptured by the art and contrivance of man.

27669.label: Acts 17:30
27669.text: True, God has overlooked the times of such ignorance, yet now he is telling mankind that they should all everywhere repent.

27670.label: Acts 17:31
27670.text: Because he has set a day in which he purposes to judge the inhabited earth in righteousness by a man whom he has appointed, and he has furnished a guarantee to all men in that he has resurrected him from the dead.”

27671.label: Acts 17:32
27671.text: Well, when they heard of a resurrection of the dead, some began to mock, while others said: “We will hear you about this even another time.”

27672.label: Acts 17:33
27672.text: Thus Paul went out from their midst,

27673.label: Acts 17:34
27673.text: but some men joined themselves to him and became believers, among whom also were Di·o·nysʹi·us, a judge of the court of the Ar·e·opʹa·gus, and a woman named Damʹa·ris, and others besides them.

27674.label: Acts 18:1
27674.text: After these things he departed from Athens and came to Corinth.

27675.label: Acts 18:2
27675.text: And he found a certain Jew named Aqʹui·la, a native of Ponʹtus who had recently come from Italy, and Pris·cilʹla his wife, because of the fact that Claudius had ordered all the Jews to depart from Rome. So he went to them

27676.label: Acts 18:3
27676.text: and on account of being of the same trade he stayed at their home, and they worked, for they were tentmakers by trade.

27677.label: Acts 18:4
27677.text: However, he would give a talk in the synagogue every sabbath and would persuade Jews and Greeks.

27678.label: Acts 18:5
27678.text: When, now, both Silas and Timothy came down from Mac·e·doʹni·a, Paul began to be intensely occupied with the word, witnessing to the Jews to prove that Jesus is the Christ.

27679.label: Acts 18:6
27679.text: But after they kept on opposing and speaking abusively, he shook out his garments and said to them: “Let YOUR blood be upon YOUR own heads. I am clean. From now on I will go to people of the nations.”

27680.label: Acts 18:7
27680.text: Accordingly he transferred from there and went into the house of a man named Titius Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house was adjoining the synagogue.

27681.label: Acts 18:8
27681.text: But Crisʹpus the presiding officer of the synagogue became a believer in the Lord, and so did all his household. And many of the Corinthians that heard began to believe and be baptized.

27682.label: Acts 18:9
27682.text: Moreover, by night the Lord said to Paul through a vision: “Have no fear, but keep on speaking and do not keep silent,

27683.label: Acts 18:10
27683.text: because I am with you and no man will assault you so as to do you injury; for I have many people in this city.”

27684.label: Acts 18:11
27684.text: So he stayed set there a year and six months, teaching among them the word of God.

27685.label: Acts 18:12
27685.text: Now while Galʹli·o was proconsul of A·chaʹia, the Jews rose up with one accord against Paul and led him to the judgment seat,

27686.label: Acts 18:13
27686.text: saying: “Contrary to the law this person leads men to another persuasion in worshiping God.”

27687.label: Acts 18:14
27687.text: But as Paul was going to open his mouth, Galʹli·o said to the Jews: “If it were, indeed, some wrong or a wicked act of villainy, O Jews, I would with reason put up patiently with YOU.

27688.label: Acts 18:15
27688.text: But if it is controversies over speech and names and the law among YOU, YOU yourselves must see to it. I do not wish to be a judge of these things.”

27689.label: Acts 18:16
27689.text: With that he drove them away from the judgment seat.

27690.label: Acts 18:17
27690.text: So they all laid hold of Sosʹthe·nes the presiding officer of the synagogue and went to beating him in front of the judgment seat. But Galʹli·o would not concern himself at all with these things.

27691.label: Acts 18:18
27691.text: However, after staying quite some days longer, Paul said good-bye to the brothers and proceeded to sail away for Syria, and with him Pris·cilʹla and Aqʹui·la, as he had the hair of his head clipped short in Cenʹchre·ae, for he had a vow.

27692.label: Acts 18:19
27692.text: So they arrived at Ephʹe·sus, and he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.

27693.label: Acts 18:20
27693.text: Although they kept requesting him to remain for a longer time, he would not consent

27694.label: Acts 18:21
27694.text: but said good-bye and told them: “I will return to YOU again, if Jehovah is willing.” And he put out to sea from Ephʹe·sus

27695.label: Acts 18:22
27695.text: and came down to Caes·a·reʹa. And he went up and greeted the congregation, and went down to Antioch.

27696.label: Acts 18:23
27696.text: And when he had passed some time there he departed and went from place to place through the country of Ga·laʹti·a and Phrygʹi·a, strengthening all the disciples.

27697.label: Acts 18:24
27697.text: Now a certain Jew named A·polʹlos, a native of Alexandria, an eloquent man, arrived in Ephʹe·sus; and he was well versed in the Scriptures.

27698.label: Acts 18:25
27698.text: This [man] had been orally instructed in the way of Jehovah and, as he was aglow with the spirit, he went speaking and teaching with correctness the things about Jesus, but being acquainted with only the baptism of John.

27699.label: Acts 18:26
27699.text: And this [man] started to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Pris·cilʹla and Aqʹui·la heard him, they took him into their company and expounded the way of God more correctly to him.

27700.label: Acts 18:27
27700.text: Further, because he was desiring to go across into A·chaʹia, the brothers wrote the disciples, exhorting them to receive him kindly. So when he got there, he greatly helped those who had believed on account of [God’s] undeserved kindness;

27701.label: Acts 18:28
27701.text: for with intensity he thoroughly proved the Jews to be wrong publicly, while he demonstrated by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.

27702.label: Acts 19:1
27702.text: In the course of events, while A·polʹlos was in Corinth, Paul went through the inland parts and came down to Ephʹe·sus, and found some disciples;

27703.label: Acts 19:2
27703.text: and he said to them: “Did you receive holy spirit when YOU became believers?” They said to him: “Why, we have never heard whether there is a holy spirit.”

27704.label: Acts 19:3
27704.text: And he said: “In what, then, were YOU baptized?” They said: “In John’s baptism.”

27705.label: Acts 19:4
27705.text: Paul said: “John baptized with the baptism [in symbol] of repentance, telling the people to believe in the one coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”

27706.label: Acts 19:5
27706.text: On hearing this, they got baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

27707.label: Acts 19:6
27707.text: And when Paul laid his hands upon them, the holy spirit came upon them, and they began speaking with tongues and prophesying.

27708.label: Acts 19:7
27708.text: All together, there were about twelve men.

27709.label: Acts 19:8
27709.text: Entering into the synagogue, he spoke with boldness for three months, giving talks and using persuasion concerning the kingdom of God.

27710.label: Acts 19:9
27710.text: But when some went on hardening themselves and not believing, speaking injuriously about The Way before the multitude, he withdrew from them and separated the disciples from them, daily giving talks in the school [auditorium] of Ty·ranʹnus.

27711.label: Acts 19:10
27711.text: This took place for two years, so that all those inhabiting the [district of] Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.

27712.label: Acts 19:11
27712.text: And God kept performing extraordinary works of power through the hands of Paul,

27713.label: Acts 19:12
27713.text: so that even cloths and aprons were borne from his body to the ailing people, and the diseases left them, and the wicked spirits came out.

27714.label: Acts 19:13
27714.text: But certain ones of the roving Jews who practiced the casting out of demons also undertook to name the name of the Lord Jesus over those having the wicked spirits, saying: “I solemnly charge YOU by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”

27715.label: Acts 19:14
27715.text: Now there were seven sons of a certain Sceʹva, a Jewish chief priest, doing this.

27716.label: Acts 19:15
27716.text: But in answer the wicked spirit said to them: “I know Jesus and I am acquainted with Paul; but who are YOU?”

27717.label: Acts 19:16
27717.text: With that the man in whom the wicked spirit was leaped upon them, got the mastery of one after the other, and prevailed against them, so that they fled naked and wounded out of that house.

27718.label: Acts 19:17
27718.text: This became known to all, both the Jews and the Greeks that dwelt in Ephʹe·sus; and a fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus went on being magnified.

27719.label: Acts 19:18
27719.text: And many of those who had become believers would come and confess and report their practices openly.

27720.label: Acts 19:19
27720.text: Indeed, quite a number of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them up before everybody. And they calculated together the prices of them and found them worth fifty thousand pieces of silver.

27721.label: Acts 19:20
27721.text: Thus in a mighty way the word of Jehovah kept growing and prevailing.

27722.label: Acts 19:21
27722.text: Now when these things had been completed, Paul purposed in his spirit that, after going through Mac·e·doʹni·a and A·chaʹia, he would journey to Jerusalem, saying: “After I get there I must also see Rome.”

27723.label: Acts 19:22
27723.text: So he dispatched to Mac·e·doʹni·a two of those who ministered to him, Timothy and E·rasʹtus, but he himself delayed for some time in the [district of] Asia.

27724.label: Acts 19:23
27724.text: At that particular time there arose no little disturbance concerning The Way.

27725.label: Acts 19:24
27725.text: For a certain man named De·meʹtri·us, a silversmith, by making silver shrines of Arʹte·mis furnished the craftsmen no little gain;

27726.label: Acts 19:25
27726.text: and he gathered them and those who worked at such things and said: “Men, YOU well know that from this business we have our prosperity.

27727.label: Acts 19:26
27727.text: Also, YOU behold and hear how not only in Ephʹe·sus but in nearly all the [district of] Asia this Paul has persuaded a considerable crowd and turned them to another opinion, saying that the ones that are made by hands are not gods.

27728.label: Acts 19:27
27728.text: Moreover, the danger exists not only that this occupation of ours will come into disrepute but also that the temple of the great goddess Arʹte·mis will be esteemed as nothing and even her magnificence which the whole [district of] Asia and the inhabited earth worships is about to be brought down to nothing.”

27729.label: Acts 19:28
27729.text: Hearing this and becoming full of anger, the men began crying out, saying: “Great is Arʹte·mis of the E·pheʹsians!”

27730.label: Acts 19:29
27730.text: So the city became filled with confusion, and with one accord they rushed into the theater, taking forcibly along with them Gaʹius and Ar·is·tarʹchus, Mac·e·doʹni·ans, traveling companions of Paul.

27731.label: Acts 19:30
27731.text: For his part, Paul was willing to go inside to the people, but the disciples would not permit him.

27732.label: Acts 19:31
27732.text: Even some of the commissioners of festivals and games, who were friendly to him, sent to him and began pleading for him not to risk himself in the theater.

27733.label: Acts 19:32
27733.text: The fact is, some were crying out one thing and others another; for the assembly was in confusion, and the majority of them did not know the reason why they had come together.

27734.label: Acts 19:33
27734.text: So together they brought Alexander out of the crowd, the Jews thrusting him up front; and Alexander motioned with his hand and was wanting to make his defense to the people.

27735.label: Acts 19:34
27735.text: But when they recognized that he was a Jew, one cry arose from them all as they shouted for about two hours: “Great is Arʹte·mis of the E·pheʹsians!”

27736.label: Acts 19:35
27736.text: When, finally, the city recorder had quieted the crowd, he said: “Men of Ephʹe·sus, who really is there of mankind that does not know that the city of the E·pheʹsians is the temple keeper of the great Arʹte·mis and of the image that fell from heaven?

27737.label: Acts 19:36
27737.text: Therefore since these things are indisputable, it is becoming for YOU to keep calm and not act rashly.

27738.label: Acts 19:37
27738.text: For YOU have brought these men who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of our goddess.

27739.label: Acts 19:38
27739.text: Therefore if De·meʹtri·us and the craftsmen with him do have a case against someone, court days are held and there are proconsuls; let them bring charges against one another.

27740.label: Acts 19:39
27740.text: If, though, YOU are searching for anything beyond that, it must be decided in a regular assembly.

27741.label: Acts 19:40
27741.text: For we are really in danger of being charged with sedition over today’s affair, no single cause existing that will permit us to render a reason for this disorderly mob.”

27742.label: Acts 19:41
27742.text: And when he had said these things, he dismissed the assembly.

27743.label: Acts 20:1
27743.text: Now after the uproar had subsided, Paul sent for the disciples, and when he had encouraged them and bidden them farewell, he went forth to journey into Mac·e·doʹni·a.

27744.label: Acts 20:2
27744.text: After going through those parts and encouraging the ones there with many a word, he came into Greece.

27745.label: Acts 20:3
27745.text: And when he had spent three months there, because a plot was hatched against him by the Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he made up his mind to return through Mac·e·doʹni·a.

27746.label: Acts 20:4
27746.text: There were accompanying him Sopʹa·ter the son of Pyrʹrhus of Be·roeʹa, Ar·is·tarʹchus and Se·cunʹdus of the Thes·sa·loʹni·ans, and Gaʹius of Derʹbe, and Timothy, and from the [district of] Asia Tychʹi·cus and Trophʹi·mus.

27747.label: Acts 20:5
27747.text: These went on and were waiting for us in Troʹas;

27748.label: Acts 20:6
27748.text: but we put out to sea from Phi·lipʹpi after the days of the unfermented cakes, and we came to them in Troʹas within five days; and there we spent seven days.

27749.label: Acts 20:7
27749.text: On the first day of the week, when we were gathered together to have a meal, Paul began discoursing to them, as he was going to depart the next day; and he prolonged his speech until midnight.

27750.label: Acts 20:8
27750.text: So there were quite a few lamps in the upper chamber where we were gathered together.

27751.label: Acts 20:9
27751.text: Seated at the window, a certain young man named Euʹty·chus fell into a deep sleep while Paul kept talking on, and, collapsing in sleep, he fell down from the third story and was picked up dead.

27752.label: Acts 20:10
27752.text: But Paul went downstairs, threw himself upon him and embraced him and said: “STOP raising a clamor, for his soul is in him.”

27753.label: Acts 20:11
27753.text: He now went upstairs and began the meal and took food, and after conversing for quite a while, until daybreak, he at length departed.

27754.label: Acts 20:12
27754.text: So they took the boy away alive and were comforted beyond measure.

27755.label: Acts 20:13
27755.text: We now went ahead to the boat and set sail to Asʹsos, where we were intending to take Paul aboard, for, after giving instructions to this effect, he himself was intending to go on foot.

27756.label: Acts 20:14
27756.text: So when he caught up with us in Asʹsos, we took him aboard and went to Mit·y·leʹne;

27757.label: Acts 20:15
27757.text: and, sailing away from there the succeeding day, we arrived opposite Chiʹos, but the next day we touched at Saʹmos, and on the following day we arrived at Mi·leʹtus.

27758.label: Acts 20:16
27758.text: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephʹe·sus, in order that he might not spend any time in the [district of] Asia; for he was hastening to get to Jerusalem on the day of the [festival of] Pentecost if he possibly could.

27759.label: Acts 20:17
27759.text: However, from Mi·leʹtus he sent to Ephʹe·sus and called for the older men of the congregation.

27760.label: Acts 20:18
27760.text: When they got to him he said to them: “YOU well know how from the first day that I stepped into the [district of] Asia I was with you the whole time,

27761.label: Acts 20:19
27761.text: slaving for the Lord with the greatest lowliness of mind and tears and trials that befell me by the plots of the Jews;

27762.label: Acts 20:20
27762.text: while I did not hold back from telling YOU any of the things that were profitable nor from teaching YOU publicly and from house to house.

27763.label: Acts 20:21
27763.text: But I thoroughly bore witness both to Jews and to Greeks about repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.

27764.label: Acts 20:22
27764.text: And now, look! bound in the spirit, I am journeying to Jerusalem, although not knowing the things that will happen to me in it,

27765.label: Acts 20:23
27765.text: except that from city to city the holy spirit repeatedly bears witness to me as it says that bonds and tribulations are waiting for me.

27766.label: Acts 20:24
27766.text: Nevertheless, I do not make my soul of any account as dear to me, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received of the Lord Jesus, to bear thorough witness to the good news of the undeserved kindness of God.

27767.label: Acts 20:25
27767.text: “And now, look! I know that all of YOU among whom I went preaching the kingdom will see my face no more.

27768.label: Acts 20:26
27768.text: Hence I call YOU to witness this very day that I am clean from the blood of all men,

27769.label: Acts 20:27
27769.text: for I have not held back from telling YOU all the counsel of God.

27770.label: Acts 20:28
27770.text: Pay attention to yourselves and to all the flock, among which the holy spirit has appointed YOU overseers, to shepherd the congregation of God, which he purchased with the blood of his own [Son].

27771.label: Acts 20:29
27771.text: I know that after my going away oppressive wolves will enter in among YOU and will not treat the flock with tenderness,

27772.label: Acts 20:30
27772.text: and from among YOU yourselves men will rise and speak twisted things to draw away the disciples after themselves.

27773.label: Acts 20:31
27773.text: “Therefore keep awake, and bear in mind that for three years, night and day, I did not quit admonishing each one with tears.

27774.label: Acts 20:32
27774.text: And now I commit YOU to God and to the word of his undeserved kindness, which [word] can build YOU up and give YOU the inheritance among all the sanctified ones.

27775.label: Acts 20:33
27775.text: I have coveted no man’s silver or gold or apparel.

27776.label: Acts 20:34
27776.text: YOU yourselves know that these hands have attended to the needs of me and of those with me.

27777.label: Acts 20:35
27777.text: I have exhibited to YOU in all things that by thus laboring YOU must assist those who are weak, and must bear in mind the words of the Lord Jesus, when he himself said, ‘There is more happiness in giving than there is in receiving.’”

27778.label: Acts 20:36
27778.text: And when he had said these things, he kneeled down with all of them and prayed.

27779.label: Acts 20:37
27779.text: Indeed, quite a bit of weeping broke out among them all, and they fell upon Paul’s neck and tenderly kissed him,

27780.label: Acts 20:38
27780.text: because they were especially pained at the word he had spoken that they were going to behold his face no more. So they proceeded to conduct him to the boat.

27781.label: Acts 21:1
27781.text: Now when we had torn ourselves away from them and put out to sea, we ran with a straight course and came to Cos, but on the next [day] to Rhodes, and from there to Patʹa·ra.

27782.label: Acts 21:2
27782.text: And when we had found a boat that was crossing to Phoe·niʹcia, we went aboard and sailed away.

27783.label: Acts 21:3
27783.text: After coming in sight of the island of Cyʹprus we left it behind on the left side and sailed on to Syria, and landed at Tyre, for there the boat was to unload [its] cargo.

27784.label: Acts 21:4
27784.text: By a search we found the disciples and remained here seven days. But through the spirit they repeatedly told Paul not to set foot in Jerusalem.

27785.label: Acts 21:5
27785.text: So when we had completed the days, we went forth and started on our way; but they all, together with the women and children, conducted us as far as outside the city. And kneeling down on the beach we had prayer

27786.label: Acts 21:6
27786.text: and said good-bye to one another, and we went up into the boat but they returned to their homes.

27787.label: Acts 21:7
27787.text: We then completed the voyage from Tyre and arrived at Ptol·e·maʹis, and we greeted the brothers and stayed one day with them.

27788.label: Acts 21:8
27788.text: The next day we set out and arrived in Caes·a·reʹa, and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelizer, who was one of the seven men, and we stayed with him.

27789.label: Acts 21:9
27789.text: This man had four daughters, virgins, that prophesied.

27790.label: Acts 21:10
27790.text: But while we were remaining quite a number of days, a certain prophet named Agʹa·bus came down from Ju·deʹa,

27791.label: Acts 21:11
27791.text: and he came to us and took up the girdle of Paul, bound his own feet and hands and said: “Thus says the holy spirit, ‘The man to whom this girdle belongs the Jews will bind in this manner in Jerusalem and deliver into the hands of people of the nations.’”

27792.label: Acts 21:12
27792.text: Now when we heard this, both we and those of that place began entreating him not to go up to Jerusalem.

27793.label: Acts 21:13
27793.text: Then Paul answered: “What are YOU doing by weeping and making me weak at heart? Rest assured, I am ready not only to be bound but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

27794.label: Acts 21:14
27794.text: When he would not be dissuaded, we acquiesced with the words: “Let the will of Jehovah take place.”

27795.label: Acts 21:15
27795.text: Now after these days we prepared for the journey and began going up to Jerusalem.

27796.label: Acts 21:16
27796.text: But some of the disciples from Caes·a·reʹa also went with us, to bring us to the man at whose home we were to be entertained, a certain Mnaʹson of Cyʹprus, an early disciple.

27797.label: Acts 21:17
27797.text: When we got into Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.

27798.label: Acts 21:18
27798.text: But on the following [day] Paul went in with us to James; and all the older men were present.

27799.label: Acts 21:19
27799.text: And he greeted them and began giving in detail an account of the things God did among the nations through his ministry.

27800.label: Acts 21:20
27800.text: After hearing this they began to glorify God, and they said to him: “You behold, brother, how many thousands of believers there are among the Jews; and they are all zealous for the Law.

27801.label: Acts 21:21
27801.text: But they have heard it rumored about you that you have been teaching all the Jews among the nations an apostasy from Moses, telling them neither to circumcise their children nor to walk in the [solemn] customs.

27802.label: Acts 21:22
27802.text: What, then, is to be done about it? In any case they are going to hear you have arrived.

27803.label: Acts 21:23
27803.text: Therefore do this which we tell you: We have four men with a vow upon themselves.

27804.label: Acts 21:24
27804.text: Take these men along and cleanse yourself ceremonially with them and take care of their expenses, that they may have their heads shaved. And so everybody will know that there is nothing to the rumors they were told about you, but that you are walking orderly, you yourself also keeping the Law.

27805.label: Acts 21:25
27805.text: As for the believers from among the nations, we have sent out, rendering our decision that they should keep themselves from what is sacrificed to idols as well as from blood and what is strangled and from fornication.”

27806.label: Acts 21:26
27806.text: Then Paul took the men along the next day and cleansed himself ceremonially with them and went into the temple, to give notice of the days to be fulfilled for the ceremonial cleansing, until the offering should be presented for each one of them.

27807.label: Acts 21:27
27807.text: Now when the seven days were about to be concluded, the Jews from Asia on beholding him in the temple began to throw all the crowd into confusion, and they laid their hands upon him,

27808.label: Acts 21:28
27808.text: crying out: “Men of Israel, help! This is the man that teaches everybody everywhere against the people and the Law and this place and, what is more, he even brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place.”

27809.label: Acts 21:29
27809.text: For they had previously seen Trophʹi·mus the E·pheʹsian in the city with him, but they were imagining Paul had brought him into the temple.

27810.label: Acts 21:30
27810.text: And the whole city was set in an uproar, and a running together of the people occurred; and they laid hold of Paul and dragged him outside the temple. And immediately the doors were closed.

27811.label: Acts 21:31
27811.text: And while they were seeking to kill him, information came up to the commander of the band that all Jerusalem was in confusion;

27812.label: Acts 21:32
27812.text: and he at once took soldiers and army officers and ran down to them. When they caught sight of the military commander and the soldiers, they quit beating Paul.

27813.label: Acts 21:33
27813.text: Then the military commander came near and took hold of him and gave command for him to be bound with two chains; and he proceeded to inquire who he might be and what he had done.

27814.label: Acts 21:34
27814.text: But some in the crowd began shouting out one thing, and others another. So, being unable himself to learn anything certain because of the tumult, he commanded him to be brought to the soldiers’ quarters.

27815.label: Acts 21:35
27815.text: But when he got upon the stairs, the situation became such that he was being carried along by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;

27816.label: Acts 21:36
27816.text: for the multitude of the people kept following, crying out: “Take him away!”

27817.label: Acts 21:37
27817.text: And as he was about to be led into the soldiers’ quarters, Paul said to the military commander: “Am I allowed to say something to you?” He said: “Can you speak Greek?

27818.label: Acts 21:38
27818.text: Are you not really the Egyptian who before these days stirred up a sedition and led the four thousand dagger men out into the wilderness?”

27819.label: Acts 21:39
27819.text: Then Paul said: “I am, in fact, a Jew, of Tarsus in Ci·liʹcia, a citizen of no obscure city. So I beg you, permit me to speak to the people.”

27820.label: Acts 21:40
27820.text: After he gave permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, motioned with his hand to the people. When a great silence fell, he addressed them in the Hebrew language, saying:

27821.label: Acts 22:1
27821.text: “Men, brothers and fathers, hear my defense to YOU now.”

27822.label: Acts 22:2
27822.text: (Well, when they heard he was addressing them in the Hebrew language, they kept all the more silent, and he said:)

27823.label: Acts 22:3
27823.text: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Ci·liʹcia, but educated in this city at the feet of Ga·maʹli·el, instructed according to the strictness of the ancestral Law, being zealous for God just as all of YOU are this day.

27824.label: Acts 22:4
27824.text: And I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and handing over to prisons both men and women,

27825.label: Acts 22:5
27825.text: as both the high priest and all the assembly of older men can bear me witness. From them I also procured letters to the brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to bring also those who were there bound to Jerusalem to be punished.

27826.label: Acts 22:6
27826.text: “But as I was journeying and drawing close to Damascus, about midday, suddenly out of heaven a great light flashed all around me,

27827.label: Acts 22:7
27827.text: and I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’

27828.label: Acts 22:8
27828.text: I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ And he said to me, ‘I am Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ, whom you are persecuting.’

27829.label: Acts 22:9
27829.text: Now the men that were with me beheld, indeed, the light but did not hear the voice of the one speaking to me.

27830.label: Acts 22:10
27830.text: At that I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me, ‘Rise, go your way into Damascus, and there you will be told about everything it is appointed for you to do.’

27831.label: Acts 22:11
27831.text: But as I could not see anything for the glory of that light, I arrived in Damascus, being led by the hand of those who were with me.

27832.label: Acts 22:12
27832.text: “Now An·a·niʹas, a certain man reverent according to the Law, well reported on by all the Jews dwelling there,

27833.label: Acts 22:13
27833.text: came to me and, standing by me, he said to me, ‘Saul, brother, have your sight again!’ And I looked up at him that very hour.

27834.label: Acts 22:14
27834.text: He said, ‘The God of our forefathers has chosen you to come to know his will and to see the righteous One and to hear the voice of his mouth,

27835.label: Acts 22:15
27835.text: because you are to be a witness for him to all men of things you have seen and heard.

27836.label: Acts 22:16
27836.text: And now why are you delaying? Rise, get baptized and wash your sins away by your calling upon his name.’

27837.label: Acts 22:17
27837.text: “But when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance

27838.label: Acts 22:18
27838.text: and saw him saying to me, ‘Hurry up and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not agree to your witness concerning me.’

27839.label: Acts 22:19
27839.text: And I said, ‘Lord, they themselves well know that I used to imprison and flog in one synagogue after another those believing upon you;

27840.label: Acts 22:20
27840.text: and when the blood of Stephen your witness was being spilled, I myself was also standing by and approving and guarding the outer garments of those doing away with him.’

27841.label: Acts 22:21
27841.text: And yet he said to me, ‘Get on your way, because I shall send you out to nations far off.’”

27842.label: Acts 22:22
27842.text: Now they kept listening to him down to this word, and they raised their voices, saying: “Take such a [man] away from the earth, for he was not fit to live!”

27843.label: Acts 22:23
27843.text: And because they were crying out and throwing their outer garments about and tossing dust into the air,

27844.label: Acts 22:24
27844.text: the military commander ordered him to be brought into the soldiers’ quarters and said he should be examined under scourging, that he might know fully for what cause they were shouting against him this way.

27845.label: Acts 22:25
27845.text: But when they had stretched him out for the whipping, Paul said to the army officer standing there: “Is it lawful for YOU men to scourge a man that is a Roman and uncondemned?”

27846.label: Acts 22:26
27846.text: Well, when the army officer heard this, he went to the military commander and made report, saying: “What are you intending to do? Why, this man is a Roman.”

27847.label: Acts 22:27
27847.text: So the military commander approached and said to him: “Tell me, Are you a Roman?” He said: “Yes.”

27848.label: Acts 22:28
27848.text: The military commander responded: “I purchased these rights as a citizen for a large sum [of money].” Paul said: “But I was even born [in them].”

27849.label: Acts 22:29
27849.text: Immediately, therefore, the men that were about to examine him with torture withdrew from him; and the military commander became afraid on ascertaining that he was a Roman and that he had bound him.

27850.label: Acts 22:30
27850.text: So, the next day, as he desired to know for sure just why he was being accused by the Jews, he let him loose and commanded the chief priests and all the Sanʹhe·drin to assemble. And he brought Paul down and stood him among them.

27851.label: Acts 23:1
27851.text: Looking intently at the Sanʹhe·drin Paul said: “Men, brothers, I have behaved before God with a perfectly clear conscience down to this day.”

27852.label: Acts 23:2
27852.text: At this the high priest An·a·niʹas ordered those standing by him to strike him on the mouth.

27853.label: Acts 23:3
27853.text: Then Paul said to him: “God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall. Do you at one and the same time sit to judge me in accord with the Law and, transgressing the Law, command me to be struck?”

27854.label: Acts 23:4
27854.text: Those standing by said: “Are you reviling the high priest of God?”

27855.label: Acts 23:5
27855.text: And Paul said: “Brothers, I did not know he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You must not speak injuriously of a ruler of your people.’”

27856.label: Acts 23:6
27856.text: Now when Paul took note that the one part was of Sadducees but the other of Pharisees, he proceeded to cry out in the Sanʹhe·drin: “Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Over the hope of resurrection of the dead I am being judged.”

27857.label: Acts 23:7
27857.text: Because he said this, a dissension arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the multitude was split.

27858.label: Acts 23:8
27858.text: For Sadducees say there is neither resurrection nor angel nor spirit, but the Pharisees publicly declare them all.

27859.label: Acts 23:9
27859.text: So there broke out a loud screaming, and some of the scribes of the party of the Pharisees rose and began contending fiercely, saying: “We find nothing wrong in this man; but if a spirit or an angel spoke to him, —.”

27860.label: Acts 23:10
27860.text: Now when the dissension grew great, the military commander became afraid that Paul would be pulled to pieces by them, and he commanded the force of soldiers to go down and snatch him from their midst and bring him into the soldiers’ quarters.

27861.label: Acts 23:11
27861.text: But the following night the Lord stood by him and said: “Be of good courage! For as you have been giving a thorough witness on the things about me in Jerusalem, so you must also bear witness in Rome.”

27862.label: Acts 23:12
27862.text: Now when it became day, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with a curse, saying they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

27863.label: Acts 23:13
27863.text: There were more than forty men that formed this oath-bound conspiracy;

27864.label: Acts 23:14
27864.text: and they went to the chief priests and the older men and said: “We have solemnly bound ourselves with a curse not to take a bite of food until we have killed Paul.

27865.label: Acts 23:15
27865.text: Now, therefore, YOU together with the Sanʹhe·drin make it clear to the military commander why he should bring him down to YOU as though YOU intended to determine more accurately the matters involving him. But before he gets near we will be ready to do away with him.”

27866.label: Acts 23:16
27866.text: However, the son of Paul’s sister heard of their lying in wait, and he came and entered into the soldiers’ quarters and reported it to Paul.

27867.label: Acts 23:17
27867.text: So Paul called one of the army officers to him and said: “Lead this young man off to the military commander, for he has something to report to him.”

27868.label: Acts 23:18
27868.text: Therefore this man took him and led him to the military commander and said: “The prisoner Paul called me to him and requested me to lead this young man to you, as he has something to tell you.”

27869.label: Acts 23:19
27869.text: The military commander took him by the hand and withdrew and began inquiring privately: “What is it you have to report to me?”

27870.label: Acts 23:20
27870.text: He said: “The Jews have agreed to request you to bring Paul down to the Sanʹhe·drin tomorrow as though intending to learn something more accurate about him.

27871.label: Acts 23:21
27871.text: Above all things, do not let them persuade you, for more than forty men of theirs are lying in wait for him, and they have bound themselves with a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they have done away with him; and they are now ready, waiting for the promise from you.”

27872.label: Acts 23:22
27872.text: Therefore the military commander let the young man go after ordering him: “Do not blab to anyone that you have made these things clear to me.”

27873.label: Acts 23:23
27873.text: And he summoned a certain two of the army officers and said: “Get two hundred soldiers ready to march clear to Caes·a·reʹa, also seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, at the third hour of the night.

27874.label: Acts 23:24
27874.text: Also, provide beasts of burden that they may have Paul ride and convey him safely to Felix the governor.”

27875.label: Acts 23:25
27875.text: And he wrote a letter having this form:

27876.label: Acts 23:26
27876.text: “Claudius Lysʹi·as to his excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings!

27877.label: Acts 23:27
27877.text: This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be done away with by them, but I came suddenly with a force of soldiers and rescued him, because I learned he was a Roman.

27878.label: Acts 23:28
27878.text: And wishing to ascertain the cause for which they were accusing him, I brought him down into their Sanʹhe·drin.

27879.label: Acts 23:29
27879.text: I found him to be accused about questions of their Law, but not charged with a single thing deserving of death or bonds.

27880.label: Acts 23:30
27880.text: But because a plot that is to be laid against the man has been disclosed to me, I am at once sending him to you, and commanding the accusers to speak against him before you.”

27881.label: Acts 23:31
27881.text: Therefore these soldiers took Paul according to their orders and brought him by night to An·tipʹa·tris.

27882.label: Acts 23:32
27882.text: The next day they permitted the horsemen to go on with him, and they returned to the soldiers’ quarters.

27883.label: Acts 23:33
27883.text: The [horsemen] entered into Caes·a·reʹa and delivered the letter to the governor and also presented Paul to him.

27884.label: Acts 23:34
27884.text: So he read it and inquired from what province he was, and ascertained that he was from Ci·liʹcia.

27885.label: Acts 23:35
27885.text: “I shall give you a thorough hearing,” he said, “when your accusers arrive also.” And he commanded that he be kept under guard in the prae·toʹri·an palace of Herod.

27886.label: Acts 24:1
27886.text: Five days later the high priest An·a·niʹas came down with some older men and a public speaker, a certain Ter·tulʹlus, and they gave information to the governor against Paul.

27887.label: Acts 24:2
27887.text: When he was called, Ter·tulʹlus started accusing him, saying: “Seeing that we enjoy great peace through you and that reforms are taking place in this nation through your forethought,

27888.label: Acts 24:3
27888.text: at all times and also in all places we receive it, Your Excellency Felix, with the greatest thankfulness.

27889.label: Acts 24:4
27889.text: But that I may not hinder you any further, I beseech you to hear us briefly in your kindliness.

27890.label: Acts 24:5
27890.text: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow and stirring up seditions among all the Jews throughout the inhabited earth and a spearhead of the sect of the Naz·a·renesʹ,

27891.label: Acts 24:6
27891.text: one who also tried to profane the temple and whom we seized.

27893.label: Acts 24:8
27893.text: From him you yourself can by examination find out about all these things of which we are accusing him.”

27894.label: Acts 24:9
27894.text: With that the Jews also joined in the attack, asserting that these things were so.

27895.label: Acts 24:10
27895.text: And Paul, when the governor nodded to him to speak, answered: “Knowing well that this nation has had you as judge for many years, I readily speak in my defense the things about myself,

27896.label: Acts 24:11
27896.text: as you are in a position to find out that for me it has not been more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem;

27897.label: Acts 24:12
27897.text: and they found me neither in the temple arguing with anyone nor causing a mob to rush together, either in the synagogues or throughout the city.

27898.label: Acts 24:13
27898.text: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they are accusing me right now.

27899.label: Acts 24:14
27899.text: But I do admit this to you, that, according to the way that they call a ‘sect,’ in this manner I am rendering sacred service to the God of my forefathers, as I believe all the things set forth in the Law and written in the Prophets;

27900.label: Acts 24:15
27900.text: and I have hope toward God, which hope these [men] themselves also entertain, that there is going to be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.

27901.label: Acts 24:16
27901.text: In this respect, indeed, I am exercising myself continually to have a consciousness of committing no offense against God and men.

27902.label: Acts 24:17
27902.text: So after quite a number of years I arrived to bring gifts of mercy to my nation, and offerings.

27903.label: Acts 24:18
27903.text: While I was at these matters they found me ceremonially cleansed in the temple, but not with a crowd or with a tumult. But there were certain Jews from the [district of] Asia,

27904.label: Acts 24:19
27904.text: who ought to be present before you and to accuse me if they might have anything against me.

27905.label: Acts 24:20
27905.text: Or, let the [men] here say for themselves what wrong they found as I stood before the Sanʹhe·drin,

27906.label: Acts 24:21
27906.text: except with respect to this one utterance which I cried out while standing among them, ‘Over the resurrection of the dead I am today being judged before YOU!’”

27907.label: Acts 24:22
27907.text: However, Felix, knowing quite accurately the matters concerning this Way, began to put the [men] off and said: “Whenever Lysʹi·as the military commander comes down, I shall decide upon these matters involving YOU.”

27908.label: Acts 24:23
27908.text: And he ordered the army officer that the man be kept and have some relaxation [of custody], and that he forbid no one of his people to wait upon him.

27909.label: Acts 24:24
27909.text: Some days later Felix arrived with Dru·silʹla his wife, who was a Jewess, and he sent for Paul and listened to him on the belief in Christ Jesus.

27910.label: Acts 24:25
27910.text: But as he talked about righteousness and self-control and the judgment to come, Felix became frightened and answered: “For the present go your way, but when I get an opportune time I shall send for you again.”

27911.label: Acts 24:26
27911.text: At the same time, though, he was hoping for money to be given him by Paul. On that account he sent for him even more frequently and would converse with him.

27912.label: Acts 24:27
27912.text: But, when two years had elapsed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus; and because Felix desired to gain favor with the Jews, he left Paul bound.

27913.label: Acts 25:1
27913.text: Therefore Festus, after entering upon the [government of the] province, went up three days later to Jerusalem from Caes·a·reʹa;

27914.label: Acts 25:2
27914.text: and the chief priests and the principal men of the Jews gave him information against Paul. So they began to entreat him,

27915.label: Acts 25:3
27915.text: asking for themselves as a favor against the [man] that he would send for him to come to Jerusalem, as they were laying an ambush to do away with him along the road.

27916.label: Acts 25:4
27916.text: However, Festus answered that Paul was to be kept in Caes·a·reʹa and that he himself was about to depart shortly for there.

27917.label: Acts 25:5
27917.text: “Hence let those who are in power among YOU,” he said, “come down with me and accuse him, if there is anything out of the way about the man.”

27918.label: Acts 25:6
27918.text: So when he had spent not more than eight or ten days among them, he went down to Caes·a·reʹa, and the next day he sat down on the judgment seat and commanded Paul to be brought in.

27919.label: Acts 25:7
27919.text: When he arrived, the Jews that had come down from Jerusalem stood round about him, leveling against him many and serious charges for which they were unable to show evidence.

27920.label: Acts 25:8
27920.text: But Paul said in defense: “Neither against the Law of the Jews nor against the temple nor against Caesar have I committed any sin.”

27921.label: Acts 25:9
27921.text: Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, said in reply to Paul: “Do you wish to go up to Jerusalem and be judged there before me concerning these things?”

27922.label: Acts 25:10
27922.text: But Paul said: “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be judged. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also are finding out quite well.

27923.label: Acts 25:11
27923.text: If, on the one hand, I am really a wrongdoer and have committed anything deserving of death, I do not beg off from dying; if, on the other hand, none of those things exists of which these [men] accuse me, no man can hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar!”

27924.label: Acts 25:12
27924.text: Then Festus, after speaking with the assembly of counselors, replied: “To Caesar you have appealed; to Caesar you shall go.”

27925.label: Acts 25:13
27925.text: Now when some days had passed, A·gripʹpa the king and Ber·niʹce arrived in Caes·a·reʹa for a visit of courtesy to Festus.

27926.label: Acts 25:14
27926.text: So, as they were spending a number of days there, Festus laid before the king the matters respecting Paul, saying: “There is a certain man left prisoner by Felix,

27927.label: Acts 25:15
27927.text: and when I was in Jerusalem the chief priests and the older men of the Jews brought information about him, asking a judgment of condemnation against him.

27928.label: Acts 25:16
27928.text: But I replied to them that it is not Roman procedure to hand any man over as a favor before the accused man meets his accusers face to face and gets a chance to speak in his defense concerning the complaint.

27929.label: Acts 25:17
27929.text: Therefore when they got together here, I made no delay, but the next day I sat down on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought in.

27930.label: Acts 25:18
27930.text: Taking the stand, the accusers produced no charge of the wicked things I had supposed concerning him.

27931.label: Acts 25:19
27931.text: They simply had certain disputes with him concerning their own worship of the deity and concerning a certain Jesus who was dead but who Paul kept asserting was alive.

27932.label: Acts 25:20
27932.text: So, being perplexed as to the dispute over these matters, I proceeded to ask if he would like to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.

27933.label: Acts 25:21
27933.text: But when Paul appealed to be kept for the decision by the August One, I commanded him to be kept until I should send him on up to Caesar.”

27934.label: Acts 25:22
27934.text: Here A·gripʹpa [said] to Festus: “I myself would also like to hear the man.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you shall hear him.”

27935.label: Acts 25:23
27935.text: Therefore, on the next day, A·gripʹpa and Ber·niʹce came with much pompous show and entered into the audience chamber together with military commanders as well as men of eminence in the city, and when Festus gave the command, Paul was brought in.

27936.label: Acts 25:24
27936.text: And Festus said: “King A·gripʹpa and all YOU men who are present with us, YOU are beholding this man concerning whom all the multitude of the Jews together have applied to me both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.

27937.label: Acts 25:25
27937.text: But I perceived he had committed nothing deserving of death. So when this [man] himself appealed to the August One, I decided to send him.

27938.label: Acts 25:26
27938.text: But concerning him I have nothing certain to write to [my] Lord. Therefore I brought him forth before YOU, and especially before you, King A·gripʹpa, in order that, after the judicial examination has taken place, I might get something to write.

27939.label: Acts 25:27
27939.text: For it seems unreasonable to me to send a prisoner and not also to signify the charges against him.”

27940.label: Acts 26:1
27940.text: A·gripʹpa said to Paul: “You are permitted to speak in behalf of yourself.” Then Paul stretched his hand out and proceeded to say in his defense:

27941.label: Acts 26:2
27941.text: “Concerning all the things of which I am accused by Jews, King A·gripʹpa, I count myself happy that it is before you I am to make my defense this day,

27942.label: Acts 26:3
27942.text: especially as you are expert on all the customs as well as the controversies among Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.

27943.label: Acts 26:4
27943.text: “Indeed, as to the manner of life from youth up that I led from [the] beginning among my nation and in Jerusalem, all the Jews

27944.label: Acts 26:5
27944.text: that have been previously acquainted with me from the first know, if they but wish to bear witness, that according to the strictest sect of our form of worship I lived a Pharisee.

27945.label: Acts 26:6
27945.text: And yet now for the hope of the promise that was made by God to our forefathers I stand called to judgment;

27946.label: Acts 26:7
27946.text: whereas our twelve tribes are hoping to attain to the fulfillment of this promise by intensely rendering him sacred service night and day. Concerning this hope I am accused by Jews, O king.

27947.label: Acts 26:8
27947.text: “Why is it judged unbelievable among YOU men that God raises up the dead?

27948.label: Acts 26:9
27948.text: I, for one, really thought within myself I ought to commit many acts of opposition against the name of Jesus the Naz·a·reneʹ;

27949.label: Acts 26:10
27949.text: which, in fact, I did in Jerusalem, and many of the holy ones I locked up in prisons, as I had received authority from the chief priests; and when they were to be executed, I cast my vote against them.

27950.label: Acts 26:11
27950.text: And by punishing them many times in all the synagogues I tried to force them to make a recantation; and since I was extremely mad against them, I went so far as to persecuting them even in outside cities.

27951.label: Acts 26:12
