27951.text: “Amid these efforts as I was journeying to Damascus with authority and a commission from the chief priests,

27952.label: Acts 26:13
27952.text: I saw at midday on the road, O king, a light beyond the brilliance of the sun flash from heaven about me and about those journeying with me.

27953.label: Acts 26:14
27953.text: And when we had all fallen to the ground I heard a voice say to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? To keep kicking against the goads makes it hard for you.’

27954.label: Acts 26:15
27954.text: But I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ And the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

27955.label: Acts 26:16
27955.text: Nevertheless, rise and stand on your feet. For to this end I have made myself visible to you, in order to choose you as an attendant and a witness both of things you have seen and things I shall make you see respecting me;

27956.label: Acts 26:17
27956.text: while I deliver you from [this] people and from the nations, to whom I am sending you,

27957.label: Acts 26:18
27957.text: to open their eyes, to turn them from darkness to light and from the authority of Satan to God, in order for them to receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by [their] faith in me.’

27958.label: Acts 26:19
27958.text: “Wherefore, King A·gripʹpa, I did not become disobedient to the heavenly sight,

27959.label: Acts 26:20
27959.text: but both to those in Damascus first and to those in Jerusalem, and over all the country of Ju·deʹa, and to the nations I went bringing the message that they should repent and turn to God by doing works that befit repentance.

27960.label: Acts 26:21
27960.text: On account of these things Jews seized me in the temple and attempted to slay me.

27961.label: Acts 26:22
27961.text: However, because I have obtained the help that is from God I continue to this day bearing witness to both small and great, but saying nothing except things the Prophets as well as Moses stated were going to take place,

27962.label: Acts 26:23
27962.text: that the Christ was to suffer and, as the first to be resurrected from the dead, he was going to publish light both to this people and to the nations.”

27963.label: Acts 26:24
27963.text: Now as he was saying these things in his defense, Festus said in a loud voice: “You are going mad, Paul! Great learning is driving you into madness!”

27964.label: Acts 26:25
27964.text: But Paul said: “I am not going mad, Your Excellency Festus, but I am uttering sayings of truth and of soundness of mind.

27965.label: Acts 26:26
27965.text: In reality, the king to whom I am speaking with freeness of speech well knows about these things; for I am persuaded that not one of these things escapes his notice, for this thing has not been done in a corner.

27966.label: Acts 26:27
27966.text: Do you, King A·gripʹpa, believe the Prophets? I know you believe.”

27967.label: Acts 26:28
27967.text: But A·gripʹpa said to Paul: “In a short time you would persuade me to become a Christian.”

27968.label: Acts 26:29
27968.text: At this Paul said: “I could wish to God that whether in a short time or in a long time not only you but also all those who hear me today would become men such as I also am, with the exception of these bonds.”

27969.label: Acts 26:30
27969.text: And the king rose and so did the governor and Ber·niʹce and the men seated with them.

27970.label: Acts 26:31
27970.text: But as they withdrew they began talking with one another, saying: “This man practices nothing deserving death or bonds.”

27971.label: Acts 26:32
27971.text: Moreover, A·gripʹpa said to Festus: “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

27972.label: Acts 27:1
27972.text: Now as it was decided for us to sail away to Italy, they proceeded to hand both Paul and certain other prisoners over to an army officer named Julius of the band of Au·gusʹtus.

27973.label: Acts 27:2
27973.text: Going aboard a boat from Ad·ra·mytʹti·um that was about to sail to places along the coast of the [district of] Asia, we set sail, there being with us Ar·is·tarʹchus a Mac·e·doʹni·an from Thes·sa·lo·niʹca.

27974.label: Acts 27:3
27974.text: And the next day we landed at Siʹdon, and Julius treated Paul with human kindness and permitted him to go to his friends and enjoy [their] care.

27975.label: Acts 27:4
27975.text: And putting out to sea from there we sailed under the [shelter of] Cyʹprus, because the winds were contrary;

27976.label: Acts 27:5
27976.text: and we navigated through the open sea along Ci·liʹcia and Pam·phylʹi·a and put into port at Myʹra in Lyʹci·a.

27977.label: Acts 27:6
27977.text: But there the army officer found a boat from Alexandria that was sailing for Italy, and he made us board it.

27978.label: Acts 27:7
27978.text: Then, after sailing on slowly quite a number of days and coming to Cniʹdus with difficulty, because the wind did not let us get on, we sailed under the [shelter of] Crete at Sal·moʹne,

27979.label: Acts 27:8
27979.text: and coasting along it with difficulty we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was the city La·seʹa.

27980.label: Acts 27:9
27980.text: As considerable time had passed and by now it was hazardous to navigate because even the fast [of atonement day] had already passed by, Paul made a recommendation,

27981.label: Acts 27:10
27981.text: saying to them: “Men, I perceive that navigation is going to be with damage and great loss not only of the cargo and the boat but also of our souls.”

27982.label: Acts 27:11
27982.text: However, the army officer went heeding the pilot and the shipowner rather than the things said by Paul.

27983.label: Acts 27:12
27983.text: Now as the harbor was inconvenient for wintering, the majority advised setting sail from there, to see if they could somehow make it to Phoenix to winter, a harbor of Crete that opens toward the northeast and toward the southeast.

27984.label: Acts 27:13
27984.text: Moreover, when the south wind blew softly, they thought they had as good as realized their purpose, and they lifted anchor and began coasting inshore along Crete.

27985.label: Acts 27:14
27985.text: After no great while, however, a tempestuous wind called Eu·ro·aqʹui·lo rushed down upon it.

27986.label: Acts 27:15
27986.text: As the boat was violently seized and was not able to keep its head against the wind, we gave way and were borne along.

27987.label: Acts 27:16
27987.text: Now we ran under [the shelter of] a certain small island called Cauʹda, and yet we were hardly able to get possession of the skiff at the stern.

27988.label: Acts 27:17
27988.text: But after hoisting it aboard they began using helps to undergird the boat; and being in fear of running aground on the Syrʹtis, they lowered the gear and thus were driven along.

27989.label: Acts 27:18
27989.text: Yet because we were being violently tossed with the tempest, the following [day] they began to lighten the ship;

27990.label: Acts 27:19
27990.text: and the third [day], with their own hands, they threw away the tackling of the boat.

27991.label: Acts 27:20
27991.text: When, now, neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no little tempest was lying upon us, all hope of our being saved finally began to be cut off.

27992.label: Acts 27:21
27992.text: And when there had been a long abstinence from food, then Paul stood up in the midst of them and said: “Men, YOU certainly ought to have taken my advice and not have put out to sea from Crete and have sustained this damage and loss.

27993.label: Acts 27:22
27993.text: Still, now I recommend to YOU to be of good cheer, for not a soul of YOU will be lost, only the boat will.

27994.label: Acts 27:23
27994.text: For this night there stood near me an angel of the God to whom I belong and to whom I render sacred service,

27995.label: Acts 27:24
27995.text: saying, ‘Have no fear, Paul. You must stand before Caesar, and, look! God has freely given you all those sailing with you.’

27996.label: Acts 27:25
27996.text: Therefore be of good cheer, men; for I believe God that it will be exactly as it has been told me.

27997.label: Acts 27:26
27997.text: However, we must be cast ashore on a certain island.”

27998.label: Acts 27:27
27998.text: Now as the fourteenth night fell and we were being tossed to and fro on the [sea of] Aʹdri·a, at midnight the sailors began to suspect they were drawing near to some land.

27999.label: Acts 27:28
27999.text: And they sounded the depth and found it twenty fathoms; so they proceeded a short distance and again made a sounding and found it fifteen fathoms.

28000.label: Acts 27:29
28000.text: And because of fearing we might be cast somewhere upon the rocks, they cast out four anchors from the stern and began wishing for it to become day.

28001.label: Acts 27:30
28001.text: But when the sailors began seeking to escape from the boat and lowered the skiff into the sea under the pretense of intending to let down anchors from the prow,

28002.label: Acts 27:31
28002.text: Paul said to the army officer and the soldiers: “Unless these men remain in the boat, YOU cannot be saved.”

28003.label: Acts 27:32
28003.text: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the skiff and let it fall off.

28004.label: Acts 27:33
28004.text: Now close to the approach of day Paul began to encourage one and all to take some food, saying: “Today is the fourteenth day YOU have been on the watch and YOU are continuing without food, having taken nothing for yourselves.

28005.label: Acts 27:34
28005.text: Therefore I encourage YOU to take some food, for this is in the interest of YOUR safety; for not a hair of the head of one of YOU will perish.”

28006.label: Acts 27:35
28006.text: After he said this, he also took a loaf, gave thanks to God before them all and broke it and started eating.

28007.label: Acts 27:36
28007.text: So they all became cheerful and themselves began taking some food.

28008.label: Acts 27:37
28008.text: Now, all together, we souls in the boat were two hundred and seventy-six.

28009.label: Acts 27:38
28009.text: When they had been satisfied with food, they proceeded to lighten the boat by throwing the wheat overboard into the sea.

28010.label: Acts 27:39
28010.text: Finally when it became day, they could not recognize the land but they were observing a certain bay with a beach, and on this they were determined, if they could, to beach the boat.

28011.label: Acts 27:40
28011.text: So, cutting away the anchors, they let them fall into the sea, at the same time loosing the lashings of the rudder oars and, after hoisting the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

28012.label: Acts 27:41
28012.text: When they lighted upon a shoal washed on each side by the sea, they ran the ship aground and the prow got stuck and stayed immovable, but the stern began to be violently broken to pieces.

28013.label: Acts 27:42
28013.text: At this it became the determination of the soldiers to kill the prisoners, that no one might swim away and escape.

28014.label: Acts 27:43
28014.text: But the army officer desired to bring Paul safely through and restrained them from their purpose. And he commanded those able to swim to cast themselves into the sea and make it to land first,

28015.label: Acts 27:44
28015.text: and the rest to do so, some upon planks and some upon certain things from the boat. And thus it came about that all were brought safely to land.

28016.label: Acts 28:1
28016.text: And when we had made it to safety, then we learned that the island was called Malta.

28017.label: Acts 28:2
28017.text: And the foreign-speaking people showed us extraordinary human kindness, for they kindled a fire and received all of us helpfully because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.

28018.label: Acts 28:3
28018.text: But when Paul collected a certain bundle of sticks and laid it upon the fire, a viper came out due to the heat and fastened itself on his hand.

28019.label: Acts 28:4
28019.text: When the foreign-speaking people caught sight of the venomous creature hanging from his hand, they began saying to one another: “Surely this man is a murderer, and although he made it to safety from the sea, vindictive justice did not permit him to keep on living.”

28020.label: Acts 28:5
28020.text: However, he shook the venomous creature off into the fire and suffered no harm.

28021.label: Acts 28:6
28021.text: But they were expecting he was going to swell up with inflammation or suddenly drop dead. After they waited for a long while and beheld nothing hurtful happen to him, they changed their mind and began saying he was a god.

28022.label: Acts 28:7
28022.text: Now in the neighborhood of that place the principal man of the island, named Pubʹli·us, had lands; and he received us hospitably and entertained us benevolently three days.

28023.label: Acts 28:8
28023.text: But it happened that the father of Pubʹli·us was lying down distressed with fever and dysentery, and Paul went in to him and prayed, laid his hands upon him and healed him.

28024.label: Acts 28:9
28024.text: After this occurred, the rest of the people on the island who had sicknesses also began to come to him and be cured.

28025.label: Acts 28:10
28025.text: And they also honored us with many gifts and, when we were setting sail, they loaded us with things for our needs.

28026.label: Acts 28:11
28026.text: Three months later we set sail in a boat from Alexandria that had wintered in the island and with the figurehead “Sons of Zeus.”

28027.label: Acts 28:12
28027.text: And putting into port at Syracuse we remained three days,

28028.label: Acts 28:13
28028.text: from which place we went around and arrived at Rheʹgi·um. And a day later a south wind sprang up and we made it into Pu·teʹo·li on the second day.

28029.label: Acts 28:14
28029.text: Here we found brothers and were entreated to remain with them seven days; and in this way we came toward Rome.

28030.label: Acts 28:15
28030.text: And from there the brothers, when they heard the news about us, came to meet us as far as the Marketplace of Apʹpi·us and Three Taverns and, upon catching sight of them, Paul thanked God and took courage.

28031.label: Acts 28:16
28031.text: When, finally, we entered into Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.

28032.label: Acts 28:17
28032.text: However, three days later he called together those who were the principal men of the Jews. When they had assembled, he proceeded to say to them: “Men, brothers, although I had done nothing contrary to the people or the customs of our forefathers, I was delivered over as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

28033.label: Acts 28:18
28033.text: And these, after making an examination, were desirous of releasing me, as there was no cause for death in me.

28034.label: Acts 28:19
28034.text: But when the Jews kept speaking against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, but not as though I had anything of which to accuse my nation.

28035.label: Acts 28:20
28035.text: Really on this account I entreated to see and speak to YOU, for because of the hope of Israel this chain I have around me.”

28036.label: Acts 28:21
28036.text: They said to him: “Neither have we received letters concerning you from Ju·deʹa, nor has anyone of the brothers that has arrived reported or spoken anything wicked about you.

28037.label: Acts 28:22
28037.text: But we think it proper to hear from you what your thoughts are, for truly as regards this sect it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”

28038.label: Acts 28:23
28038.text: They now arranged for a day with him, and they came in greater numbers to him in his lodging place. And he explained the matter to them by bearing thorough witness concerning the kingdom of God and by using persuasion with them concerning Jesus from both the law of Moses and the Prophets, from morning till evening.

28039.label: Acts 28:24
28039.text: And some began to believe the things said; others would not believe.

28040.label: Acts 28:25
28040.text: So, because they were at disagreement with one another, they began to depart, while Paul made this one comment: “The holy spirit aptly spoke through Isaiah the prophet to YOUR forefathers,

28041.label: Acts 28:26
28041.text: saying, ‘Go to this people and say: “By hearing, YOU will hear but by no means understand; and, looking, YOU will look but by no means see.

28042.label: Acts 28:27
28042.text: For the heart of this people has grown unreceptive, and with their ears they have heard without response, and they have shut their eyes; that they should never see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I should heal them.”’

28043.label: Acts 28:28
28043.text: Therefore let it be known to YOU that this, the means by which God saves, has been sent out to the nations; they will certainly listen to it.”

28045.label: Acts 28:30
28045.text: So he remained for an entire two years in his own hired house, and he would kindly receive all those who came in to him,

28046.label: Acts 28:31
28046.text: preaching the kingdom of God to them and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with the greatest freeness of speech, without hindrance.
